# e2e: agentic end-to-end tests

e2e runs UI tests that mix agent goals with exact steps. `agent.act` drives
one goal; `agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`, and `agent.extract` judge the
screen; `screen`, `app`, `browser`, and `expect` act and check exactly. UI
targets use `@e2e-dev/web` for browsers or `@e2e-dev/mobile` for iOS
simulators, Android emulators, and connected phones.

## Start here: pick the reference for the job

Read the one reference that matches the request before doing anything else.
Each stands on its own; a reference names another topic only for a side
trip. `npx e2e guide <topic>` prints the installed package's version of a
reference; prefer it when it differs from this copy.
The Rules and Feedback sections below still apply.

| When you are | Topic | Read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adding e2e to a project, writing `e2e.config.ts`, starting the app from the config, signing in to a model, setting up mobile targets | `setup` | [references/setup.md](references/setup.md) |
| Looking at the running app, checking a UI change, taking a screenshot or video, trying a locator, running a test line, or walking a flow while you write its test, over `e2e mcp` | `mcp` | [references/mcp.md](references/mcp.md) |

## Quick start

A config with one web target and a model, and a test that drives one goal
and pins the outcome:

```ts
// e2e.config.ts
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { gateway } from 'ai';

export default {
  targets: [
    {
      engine: web(),
      app: {
        url: 'http://127.0.0.1:3000',
        command: { executable: 'pnpm', args: ['dev'], log: '.e2e/logs/app.log' },
      },
    },
  ],
  // The model behind every agent.* step: an AI SDK instance; gateway() from 'ai' reads AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY or a Vercel OIDC token.
  agents: {
    default: {
      model: gateway('openai/gpt-6-luna-fast'),
      system: 'You are a thorough QA agent. Verify every outcome on screen.',
    },
  },
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

```ts
// tests/billing.e2e.ts
import { describe, test } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { expect } from 'e2e';

describe('billing', () => {
  test('a member upgrades to Pro', async ({ app, agent, screen, browser }) => {
    await app.open('/settings/billing');

    await agent.act('upgrade the workspace to the Pro plan');

    await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toContainText('Pro');
    await expect(browser).toHaveURL('/settings/billing');
  });
});
```

## Workflow: writing a test

1. Look at what exists: `e2e.config.ts`, `.mts`, `.js`, or `.mjs`, the `tests` glob
   (default `tests/**/*.e2e.ts`), `e2e` in `package.json`. Nothing there:
   follow `setup` when the user has requested e2e (see Rules).
2. With a connected `e2e mcp` server (topic `mcp`), write the test while
   you walk the flow, not from memory after the walk. A test written
   afterwards fails on each name or step you got wrong, one run at a time.
   Before `open_session`, create `tests/<feature>.e2e.ts`, opening on the
   screen it covers (step 3). Then add each step to the file as you take it
   in the session. An `act` goal goes in before you walk its path, and the
   path's actions stay out of the test. A `screen` line is the `Test line:`
   its action printed, copied as is. When the outcome shows, run its
   `expect` with `run_code` and add it once it passes; a passing statement
   also joins `test_lines`; checks go in the test's assert block at the end.
   The walk ends with the test written. Without a
   server, learn the accessible names the app renders from the components or
   a `--headed` run.
3. Shape the file before the steps (topic `writing-tests`, "Structure"):
   one top-level `describe` per feature, and in it one test per behavior,
   titled with the outcome it verifies. Each test runs arrange, act, assert,
   in that order: reach the starting state, do the one thing under test,
   then every `expect` or `agent.assert` at the end. A second outcome worth
   checking is a second test, so a failing title says what broke.
   A step is an `agent.act` goal or `screen` lines. Drive the flow with
   `agent.act`, one atomic goal per call; three goals make three calls.
   Start the test on the screen it covers, since every rerun pays
   for the steps before: in a browser a saved session instead of the
   sign-in form and `app.open` on that screen's path, on a device
   `device.openLink`, and data from the app's API (topic `writing-tests`).
   Exact values go through `screen`: a sign-in form in a setup test, a field
   that must receive one specific string, a count that must be one number.
4. Run only the test you are working on:
   `npx e2e run tests/<feature>.e2e.ts:<line>` (over MCP,
   `run_tests {files: ["tests/<feature>.e2e.ts:<line>"]}`, the flags as
   camelCase fields such as `retries: 0`), the line its `test(` opens on,
   with the flags in "Rerunning a test while you fix it" below. Agent
   steps need a model in the config and that provider's authentication (a
   saved subscription login, an API key); a local endpoint may need none.
   Tests without agent steps need no model.
5. When it fails, fix it from what the run recorded (next section).

## Workflow: fixing a failed test

The run already saw every screen up to the failure. Fix from what it
recorded; never walk the flow again from the start over MCP just to see a
screen.

1. Read the failure block in the terminal: the failing line with its code
   frame, the message (an assertion's `expected` and `observed`), where the
   screen was (`❯ at`: a URL on the web, the app and screen title on a
   device), and the nodes nearest a failed locator (`❯ on screen`). Then
   read the trace page it names (`❯ trace .e2e/results/<test>/trace.md`):
   every step with what it did, what the app logged, the agent's turns, and
   `## Screen at failure`, the screen one node per line (topic `debugging`).
2. Fix every line that evidence covers, not only the one that failed: the
   screen at failure shows the names the rest of that screen's lines need.
   Fix the locator, the expectation, or the app. Never add a sleep or a
   fixed delay (`setTimeout`, `waitForTimeout`): wait for the state you
   need with `agent.waitFor('<that state>')` instead (topic `agent`; it
   needs a model).
3. A test stops at its first failed step (an `expect.soft` lets it go on),
   and every wrong line after it costs another run. Before rerunning, check
   the lines after it as far as you can: against the screen at failure, the
   app source, or a live session.
4. For a screen the evidence and the source leave out, look live (topic
   `mcp`). `open_session {test: "tests/<feature>.e2e.ts"}` (with `:<line>`
   of its `test(` call when the file holds several) runs the test and stops
   on the live screen where it failed. Act out the lines after it there and
   put the `Test line:` each action prints in place of a wrong one, so the
   next rerun catches every mistake. Otherwise open or reuse a session, go
   straight to that screen, then `observe` and `locate`, or `run_code` for
   the fixed line and the ones after it. On the web, `navigate` to the path
   of the `❯ at` URL or the screen's route, and tap only to reach a state no
   URL opens. A device session starts on the app's launch screen: take the
   shortest path from there.
5. Rerun only that test, the way the next section says, or in a new
   session with `open_session {test}` (topic `mcp` says when a session
   must close first). Repeat with the next failure.

## Rerunning a test while you fix it

Every run of a failing test waits out its failure, and every `agent.act`
that runs live spends model calls. Keep each rerun to the one test and the
lines you changed:

- Run by `file:line`, not the file or the suite. After an edit above the
  test, look its `test(` line up again: a stale line runs another test, or
  fails with `NO_TESTS` listing the lines tests start at.
- Add `--action-timeout 5000`: a locator that matches nothing fails in 5 s
  instead of the default 30 s. It also bounds each action inside an agent
  step, so keep it longer than the slowest screen takes to load. A `screen`
  call's own `{ timeout }` still wins. An `expect` already gives up after
  5 s by default (`assertionTimeout`).
- Keep the replay cache on. A failed run keeps the recording of every goal
  a later check or wait confirmed (the wait closing the arrange block, topic
  `writing-tests`), and the next run replays those with no model call.
  New, changed, and failed goals run live, and so does a replay the trace
  page shows as handed off. `agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`, and
  `agent.extract` always call the model. Leave `--no-cache` off: it sends every goal to the model
  again. Only a `read-write` cache records: the local default, but not with
  `CI` set and no cache mode in the config, nor in strict mode. A stopped
  run (Ctrl-C, a command your tool's timeout kills, `--max-duration`) saves
  nothing, so give the command a timeout longer than the test.
- Don't rename the test, its `describe`, or its file, and don't reword a
  goal, change its params, or change the agent's `context` or the test's
  `agentContext` once a goal passes. Each is part of a recording's key, so
  every goal it touches records again live. Fixing a locator or an
  expectation keeps the recordings.
- Add `--retries 0` when retries are on (`retries` in the config, or `CI`
  set, where the default is 1); a `retries` option on the test or its
  `describe` wins over the flag. Outside strict mode (`--strict-cache`, `cache.strict`), a
  retry never replays: it runs every goal live and waits out the failure
  again.
- Once the test passes, drop `--action-timeout` and run it one time with
  `--no-cache`: every goal runs live at the config's timeouts, which shows
  the agent still reaches it without its recordings.

## Rules

- In a project without e2e, set it up when the user requests it. Otherwise
  ask before adding a test framework, and name any existing framework.
- Live MCP tools need an `e2e mcp` server in the client: the e2e plugin's, or
  one registered in the project (topic `mcp`). In a directory with no e2e config, a live look still
  works: `open_session {engine: "@e2e-dev/web", app: {url: "http://localhost:3000"}}` opens a session
  on the engine's defaults. Tests need a config. Tests run with the CLI, or with the server's
  `run_tests`, the same run without a shell.
  Keep a session open across runs while you write or fix a web test; topic
  `mcp` says when a run can go beside it, and what to do on
  `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`.
- Run the CLI as `npx e2e ...` (or `pnpm exec e2e ...`).
- The config is `export default { ... } satisfies E2EConfig` with
  `import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e'`. `targets` is required; a UI target
  names an engine and declares the app beside it: `{ engine: web(), app: { url, command } }`.
  A tools-only target can omit the engine and set `platform`.
- Import `test`, `describe`, the hooks, `expect`, `credentials`, and
  `secrets` from `e2e`. A test that uses the `browser` fixture imports `test`,
  `describe`, and the hooks from `@e2e-dev/web`: the same runtime functions,
  typed with `browser`.
- Config and tests are ES modules whatever `package.json` sets as `type`.
- Locators resolve when used. Actions wait for readiness and `expect` retries
  assertions. Reads such as `textContent()` wait for one match until the
  action timeout, then answer the current value; `count()` and `isVisible()`
  answer from the current screen. Nothing waits for a value to change, so use
  a matcher when a value has to settle.
- A locator that matches two nodes fails with `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`; narrow it
  (topic `writing-tests`).
- Secrets never appear in test code. Declare accounts under `credentials` and
  every other sensitive value under `secrets` in the config; resolve with
  `credentials.user(name).password` or `secrets.get(name)` (separate
  namespaces: `secrets.get` never returns a password), and hand the opaque
  `Secret` only to `fill()` or `agent.act` params.
- Tests: one top-level `describe` per feature, one behavior per test,
  arrange, act, assert with every assertion last (topic `writing-tests`).
  Bad: one test that adds a todo, checks it, marks it done, and checks
  again. Good: `'adds a todo to the list'` and `'marks a todo as done'`,
  the second adding its todo in its arrange block.
- Agent instructions: one goal per `act`, the wording on screen, real values
  in params. A goal is atomic: one outcome that one check confirms. Two
  outcomes are two goals in two `act` calls (topic `agent`), never `'add a
  todo and mark it done'`. Judge meaning, not phrasing: `toContain('Pro')`,
  not an exact sentence a model produced.
- End every test that runs an agent goal with a verifying check: a
  locator matcher (`expect(locator)`), an engine matcher
  (`expect(browser).toHaveURL`), or `agent.assert`. A passing one confirms
  every `act` before it, so they can be cached and replayed without model
  calls, and so do `locator.waitFor`, `browser.waitForURL`, and
  `agent.waitFor`. Reads, `expect.poll`, and plain-value `expect` confirm
  nothing (topic `agent`, "The replay cache").
- Shape the agent for this app: `context` for vocabulary the screens use,
  `system` for how it works, tools for a test API, named personas under
  `agents`. When a step fails, tighten the goal first, then the context, then
  the agent.
- `.e2e/` is output (`report.json`, `results/`, `cache/`, `logs/`; the
  config's `output` moves the report and artifacts, never `cache/` or the
  app's log). Read it, never edit it.

## Feedback

When e2e itself gets in your way, offer to tell the e2e team: a command or
API that broke (`bug`), docs or this skill that misled you (`docs`), or a
capability you needed and did not find (`feature`). Once per problem, after
you worked around it or gave up. Never report:

- failures of the app under test, or its own behavior;
- a problem you saw once and could not see again;
- anything on an outdated e2e: the command refuses it, so upgrade
  (`npx e2e@latest upgrade`) and check the problem still happens first.

Search [existing issues](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/issues) first
(`gh issue list -R e2e-inc/e2e --search "<words>"`); comment on a match
instead of sending a new report.

A `bug` needs `--repro`, steps that reproduce it every time without app
content. Without such steps, or when the bug needs your app to show, omit
`--repro`: the command then prints a prefilled GitHub issue and sends
nothing; show the user the link and tell them to add a minimal reproduction
and submit it. Never file the issue yourself.

Run it with `--dry-run` first, show the user what would be sent, and send
it only when they agree.

```bash
npx e2e feedback --type bug -m "<one or two sentences>" \
  --repro "<steps that reproduce it every time>" --error-code LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS \
  --task "<what you were doing>" --expected "<...>" --actual "<error message>" \
  --approach "<what you tried>" --command "<e2e command>" --agent "<agent / model>"
```

Describe e2e's behavior only, briefly: never paste app content, page text,
test files, URLs of private apps, or credentials. Secret-named environment
variables and common token shapes are redacted, but do not rely on it. After
sending, give the user the reference id it prints.

   and every wrong line after it costs another run. Before rerunning, check
   the lines after it as far as you can: against the screen at failure, the
   app source, or a live session.
4. For a screen the evidence and the source leave out, look live (topic
   `mcp`). `open_session {test: "tests/<feature>.e2e.ts"}` (with `:<line>`
   of its `test(` call when the file holds several) runs the test and stops
   on the live screen where it failed. Act out the lines after it there and
   put the `Test line:` each action prints in place of a wrong one, so the
   next rerun catches every mistake. Otherwise open or reuse a session, go
   straight to that screen, then `observe` and `locate`, or `run_code` for
   the fixed line and the ones after it. On the web, `navigate` to the path
   of the `❯ at` URL or the screen's route, and tap only to reach a state no
   URL opens. A device session starts on the app's launch screen: take the
   shortest path from there.
5. Rerun only that test, the way the next section says, or in a new
   session with `open_session {test}` (topic `mcp` says when a session
   must close first). Repeat with the next failure.

## Rerunning a test while you fix it

Every run of a failing test waits out its failure, and every `agent.act`
that runs live spends model calls. Keep each rerun to the one test and the
lines you changed:

- Run by `file:line`, not the file or the suite. After an edit above the
  test, look its `test(` line up again: a stale line runs another test, or
  fails with `NO_TESTS` listing the lines tests start at.
- Add `--action-timeout 5000`: a locator that matches nothing fails in 5 s
  instead of the default 30 s. It also bounds each action inside an agent
  step, so keep it longer than the slowest screen takes to load. A `screen`
  call's own `{ timeout }` still wins. An `expect` already gives up after
  5 s by default (`assertionTimeout`).
- Keep the replay cache on. A failed run keeps the recording of every goal
  a later check or wait confirmed (the wait closing the arrange block, topic
  `writing-tests`), and the next run replays those with no model call.
  New, changed, and failed goals run live, and so does a replay the trace
  page shows as handed off. `agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`, and
  `agent.extract` always call the model. Leave `--no-cache` off: it sends every goal to the model
  again. Only a `read-write` cache records: the local default, but not with
  `CI` set and no cache mode in the config, nor in strict mode. A stopped
  run (Ctrl-C, a command your tool's timeout kills, `--max-duration`) saves
  nothing, so give the command a timeout longer than the test.
- Don't rename the test, its `describe`, or its file, and don't reword a
  goal, change its params, or change the agent's `context` or the test's
  `agentContext` once a goal passes. Each is part of a recording's key, so
  every goal it touches records again live. Fixing a locator or an
  expectation keeps the recordings.
- Add `--retries 0` when retries are on (`retries` in the config, or `CI`
  set, where the default is 1); a `retries` option on the test or its
  `describe` wins over the flag. Outside strict mode (`--strict-cache`, `cache.strict`), a
  retry never replays: it runs every goal live and waits out the failure
  again.
- Once the test passes, drop `--action-timeout` and run it one time with
  `--no-cache`: every goal runs live at the config's timeouts, which shows
  the agent still reaches it without its recordings.

## Rules

- In a project without e2e, set it up when the user requests it. Otherwise
  ask before adding a test framework, and name any existing framework.
- Live MCP tools need an `e2e mcp` server in the client: the e2e plugin's, or
  one registered in the project (topic `mcp`). In a directory with no e2e config, a live look still
  works: `open_session {engine: "@e2e-dev/web", app: {url: "http://localhost:3000"}}` opens a session
  on the engine's defaults. Tests need a config. Tests run with the CLI, or with the server's
  `run_tests`, the same run without a shell.
  Keep a session open across runs while you write or fix a web test; topic
  `mcp` says when a run can go beside it, and what to do on
  `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`.
- Run the CLI as `npx e2e ...` (or `pnpm exec e2e ...`).
- The config is `export default { ... } satisfies E2EConfig` with
  `import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e'`. `targets` is required; a UI target
  names an engine and declares the app beside it: `{ engine: web(), app: { url, command } }`.
  A tools-only target can omit the engine and set `platform`.
- Import `test`, `describe`, the hooks, `expect`, `credentials`, and
  `secrets` from `e2e`. A test that uses the `browser` fixture imports `test`,
  `describe`, and the hooks from `@e2e-dev/web`: the same runtime functions,
  typed with `browser`.
- Config and tests are ES modules whatever `package.json` sets as `type`.
- Locators resolve when used. Actions wait for readiness and `expect` retries
  assertions. Reads such as `textContent()` wait for one match until the
  action timeout, then answer the current value; `count()` and `isVisible()`
  answer from the current screen. Nothing waits for a value to change, so use
  a matcher when a value has to settle.
- A locator that matches two nodes fails with `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`; narrow it
  (topic `writing-tests`).
- Secrets never appear in test code. Declare accounts under `credentials` and
  every other sensitive value under `secrets` in the config; resolve with
  `credentials.user(name).password` or `secrets.get(name)` (separate
  namespaces: `secrets.get` never returns a password), and hand the opaque
  `Secret` only to `fill()` or `agent.act` params.
- Tests: one top-level `describe` per feature, one behavior per test,
  arrange, act, assert with every assertion last (topic `writing-tests`).
  Bad: one test that adds a todo, checks it, marks it done, and checks
  again. Good: `'adds a todo to the list'` and `'marks a todo as done'`,
  the second adding its todo in its arrange block.
- Agent instructions: one goal per `act`, the wording on screen, real values
  in params. A goal is atomic: one outcome that one check confirms. Two
  outcomes are two goals in two `act` calls (topic `agent`), never `'add a
  todo and mark it done'`. Judge meaning, not phrasing: `toContain('Pro')`,
  not an exact sentence a model produced.
- End every test that runs an agent goal with a verifying check: a
  locator matcher (`expect(locator)`), an engine matcher
  (`expect(browser).toHaveURL`), or `agent.assert`. A passing one confirms
  every `act` before it, so they can be cached and replayed without model
  calls, and so do `locator.waitFor`, `browser.waitForURL`, and
  `agent.waitFor`. Reads, `expect.poll`, and plain-value `expect` confirm
  nothing (topic `agent`, "The replay cache").
- Shape the agent for this app: `context` for vocabulary the screens use,
  `system` for how it works, tools for a test API, named personas under
  `agents`. When a step fails, tighten the goal first, then the context, then
  the agent.
- `.e2e/` is output (`report.json`, `results/`, `cache/`, `logs/`; the
  config's `output` moves the report and artifacts, never `cache/` or the
  app's log). Read it, never edit it.

## Feedback

When e2e itself gets in your way, offer to tell the e2e team: a command or
API that broke (`bug`), docs or this skill that misled you (`docs`), or a
capability you needed and did not find (`feature`). Once per problem, after
you worked around it or gave up. Never report:

- failures of the app under test, or its own behavior;
- a problem you saw once and could not see again;
- anything on an outdated e2e: the command refuses it, so upgrade
  (`npx e2e@latest upgrade`) and check the problem still happens first.

Search [existing issues](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e/issues) first
(`gh issue list -R e2e-inc/e2e --search "<words>"`); comment on a match
instead of sending a new report.

A `bug` needs `--repro`, steps that reproduce it every time without app
content. Without such steps, or when the bug needs your app to show, omit
`--repro`: the command then prints a prefilled GitHub issue and sends
nothing; show the user the link and tell them to add a minimal reproduction
and submit it. Never file the issue yourself.

Run it with `--dry-run` first, show the user what would be sent, and send
it only when they agree.

```bash
npx e2e feedback --type bug -m "<one or two sentences>" \
  --repro "<steps that reproduce it every time>" --error-code LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS \
  --task "<what you were doing>" --expected "<...>" --actual "<error message>" \
  --approach "<what you tried>" --command "<e2e command>" --agent "<agent / model>"
```

Describe e2e's behavior only, briefly: never paste app content, page text,
test files, URLs of private apps, or credentials. Secret-named environment
variables and common token shapes are redacted, but do not rely on it. After
sending, give the user the reference id it prints.

# Agent steps

`agent` is a fixture like `screen` and the main way a test drives the app.
Each call is one bounded invocation: fresh redacted observation, deadline,
model-call budget, no shared transcript. No agent step, no model calls.

## Contents

- Configure a model
- act: one goal
- assert, waitFor, extract: one question
- Write instructions the model can execute
- What the model sees
- Budgets and cost
- The replay cache
- Inspect what the model did
- Make the agent yours
- Beyond the built-in agent
- In CI

## Configure a model

Put an AI SDK model under `agents.default`. You can use all AI SDK providers
that support tool calls and the language model specification v2 or later
(https://ai-sdk.dev/providers). Examples: `@ai-sdk/openai`,
`@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `@ai-sdk/google`, `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock`,
`@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider`, `ollama-ai-provider-v2`. For a server with
`/v1/chat/completions`, use `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. Vercel AI Gateway
reads `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` or, without it, a Vercel OIDC token:

```ts
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { gateway } from 'ai';

export default {
  targets: [{ engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:3000' } }],
  agents: { default: { model: gateway('openai/gpt-6-luna-fast') } },
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

Subscription logins and local models: topic `setup`, section "Subscriptions
and API keys". Keep `ai@^7` installed with any provider.

Decision models pick actions from choices the executor builds: install
`@e2e-dev/decision` and put `decisionExecutor({ model:
typeSafeAi.decisionModel('jev-latest'), textModel: openrouter('inception/mercury-2.5') })`
under `executor`. `openai.decisionModel('gpt-6-luna')` from `@ai-sdk/openai`
4.0.90 or later works too and takes the `vision: true` screenshot.
Tests stay plain language with no params. The text model writes field values
and upload paths. See the shipped `docs/decision-models.mdx` or
[the online guide](https://e2e.com/docs/decision-models) for setup,
gates, and limits.

A coding agent the user already signs in to runs agent steps over the Agent Client Protocol:
install `@e2e-dev/acp` and its adapter, and put
`claudeCode({ model: 'sonnet' })` or `codex()` under
`executor`; no model provider is needed. See the shipped `docs/subscriptions.mdx` or
[the online guide](https://e2e.com/docs/subscriptions#use-your-coding-agent).

- Pass a model instance, not a string (`INVALID_CONFIG`).
- An agents entry is one plain object of `model`, `judge`, `system`,
  `context`, `tools`, `maxSteps`, `maxModelCalls`, `judgmentTimeout`,
  `maxObservationBytes`, `maxInputTokens`, `providerOptions`, or `executor`
  for a custom brain; none inherits `model` or `context` from `default`.
- `model` drives `agent.act`. Judgments use `judge` when set, else `model`.
- A missing model for the built-in agent raises one run-level
  `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` when the first test acquires `agent`, exit 2, and so
  does a model GitHub Copilot does not serve to the account, at the first
  call; auth failures surface on the first model call as
  `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`, or as `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED` for a provider that
  reads its key when the config loads.
- `context` is what the app calls things, sent to every model call, judges
  included; `system` is how the acting agent works, read only by the act
  loop. Both live on the agents entry; `agentContext` on a test or group
  adds more. Under `e2e run`, every prompt carries the test's title path
  (`Test: billing > upgrades the tier`), judges included, so name a test
  for what it covers, not for the verdict it expects.

### Choose an agent

Tests use `agents.default` unless selected otherwise:

- `e2e run --agent buyer` picks another configured agent.
- `{ agent: 'buyer' }` on a test or group pins that agent; a list such as
  `{ agent: ['buyer', 'admin'] }` runs each test once per agent.
- `--agent buyer,admin` runs unpinned tests for both, narrows a pinned list
  to matching names, never replacing a pin it does not name.
- `{ agent: 'name' }` on an `agent.*` call overrides the test's choice.

For signed-in personas, pair an agent with a `session` in a describe block
repeated per persona; the cache keys every entry by the agent and its
context, so each persona records and replays its own steps.

## act: one goal

```ts
import { credentials } from 'e2e';

await agent.act('add a todo named "Buy milk"');
await agent.act('invite {email} as an editor', { params: { email: 'ada@example.test' } });

const member = credentials.user('member');
await agent.act('sign in with the given credentials', {
  params: {
    username: member.username,
    password: member.password, // a Secret: the model sees its name, the runner fills the field
  },
});
```

`act(instruction, options?)` runs a multi-action flow to a verdict. Passed
resolves with `summary`, `modelCalls`, `actions`, and `cache` (the replay
cache's part). Failed or blocked throws an `AgentError` whose `code` says
why: `ACTION_FAILED` (product failure); `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`,
`STEP_TIMEOUT`, `CONTEXT_OVERFLOW` (out of room);
`AUTH_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE`, `AUTH_CREDENTIAL_INVALID`,
`SECRET_UNAVAILABLE`, `ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE`, `SEED_DATA_MISSING`,
`TEST_SETUP_FAILED`, `AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED`, `POLICY_DENIED` (blocked
from outside);
`MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` (unusable answer), `MODEL_REFUSED` (the model refused
the prompt). Full list: topic debugging.

Options:

- `params`: values the instruction names; the runner fills a `Secret`,
  and a run-unique `unique(\`E2E ${Date.now()}\`)` keeps the cache working
  across runs.
- `timeout`: the config `timeout`.
- `maxSteps` (default 25 actions), `maxModelCalls` (default 25): may only
  lower the agent's limits, else `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.
- No `schema` (use `extract({ schema })`) and no `vision`: the model decides
  when it needs pixels.

The tools, one per engine action. Name the target as the screen names it
(files in `params`); the agent picks the verb:

- `observe`: re-read the screen after waiting on work in progress.
- `tap`: button, link, menu item, tab, checkbox, row, field.
- `double_tap`/`long_press`/`right_click`: second-click item, long-press
  menu, context menu only.
- `hover`: menus, flyouts, tooltips that open on the pointer.
- `type`: one input; on browser/device no target means focus; `replace` clears.
- `press`: one key to a node or, on browser/device, to focus; `times` up to 20.
- `select`: one option by visible label.
- `check`: set a checkbox, switch, or radio to a state, not flip it.
- `scroll`: viewport or one scrollable node, a screen or a few.
- `scroll_to`: a listed node into view, or by `text` page a list to a row.
- `drag`: one node onto another.
- `upload`: project-root files, or e2e's samples (`sample:photo.png`,
  `sample:document.pdf`, and the rest) when the step names none, to a file
  input or a visible control that opens a native file chooser; outside the
  root or hidden (`.env`) is `POLICY_DENIED`.
- `navigate`: a URL or app-relative path.
- `back`: browser history or in-app back.
- `resize_viewport`: set the viewport size (200 to 4096 CSS px) to check a
  layout at phone, tablet, or desktop width. Engines with `session.resize`,
  such as web.
- `switch_tab`: show another open tab by its number (from 1, in opening
  order). A tab the app opens stays in the background: the action's result
  says so, and the screen header says `tab 1 of 2`. Engines with
  `session.switchTab`, such as web.
- `close_tab`: close an open tab by the same number. Closing the tab on
  screen returns the screen to its opener, or to the tab shown most
  recently when the opener is closed too. The last open tab stays open.
  Engines with `session.closeTab`, such as web.
- `type_secret`: a declared secret by name; plaintext never reaches the model.
  Offered whenever the engine can fill secrets; the step's opening message
  lists the ones it declares, and an undeclared name fills nothing.
- `screenshot`: attach viewport pixels; every later result then carries one.
- `tap_at`/`hover_at`/`press_at`/`select_at`/`type_at`: a screenshot point.
- `drag_at`: from one screenshot point to another (`to_x`, `to_y`).
- `dismiss_keyboard` (device): hide the on-screen keyboard.

The focused field's selected text is listed as `selection="..."` (never for
a secret), so a repeated `Shift+ArrowLeft` selects one word with visible
feedback. Point tools serve a canvas shape, map pin, image region, or system
sheet control. `tap_at`, `hover_at`, and `drag_at` act at the point
(`drag_at` by id between two different listed controls on an engine without
a bare-point drag); `press_at`, `select_at`, and `type_at` hit-test the
tree first so a listed control underneath is acted on by id, and `type_at`
on nothing listed taps, then types. A screen with
nothing to tap by id opens with a screenshot attached. A device has no
`right_click`, `select`, `upload`, or `scroll_to` by node id. Pixels mask
secure fields only (topic writing-tests). A result says when an action
closed an on-screen keyboard; on a touch screen that tap was often spent
closing it, so act again.

## assert, waitFor, extract: one question

```ts
import { z } from 'zod';

await agent.assert('the dashboard shows a trial badge'); // one look, one judgment

await agent.waitFor('the export finished and a download link appeared', { // polls
  interval: 500,
  timeout: 120_000,
});

const data = await agent.extract('every todo title and how many remain', { // structured output
  schema: z.object({ titles: z.array(z.string()), remaining: z.number().int() }),
});
expect(data.titles).toContain('Buy milk');
```

- `assert` does not poll. False is `ASSERTION_FAILED` with the model's
  explanation and a screenshot in the report; too little on screen to
  decide is `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE`, also a failure, so reach the right
  screen first and ask about what is visible. Judged from the tree alone,
  it adds `pass vision: true when the answer is in pixels`, as does
  `waitFor`'s timeout after an inconclusive round.
- Judgments see the assertion, its params, the agent's context, the test
  title, and the current screen with its location, never prior steps or the act loop's
  summaries; malformed output gets one repair round, then
  `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID`.
- `assert` and `waitFor` take `params` like `act`:
  `assert('the table lists {name}', { params: { name } })`. The judge sees a
  `Secret` by name only; check a secret's value with a locator assertion.
- A value shown in more than one place (a total in the summary and on the
  pay button) must agree everywhere, or the judgment fails. Name the one
  you mean (`'the order summary total is $42.00'`) when only it matters.
- `waitFor` observes every 500 ms, judges only when the screen or its
  location changed, and is `STEP_TIMEOUT` after `timeout` (default 30 s). A
  change after a still screen is judged at once; while the screen keeps
  changing, at most once per `interval` (default 3 s).
- Never sleep for a fixed time to let the app settle. A sleep is too short
  on a slow run and wasted time on a fast one; `waitFor` returns as soon as
  the state appears:

```ts
// BAD: guesses how long the export takes.
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 10_000));

// GOOD: waits for the state, up to the timeout.
await agent.waitFor('the export finished and a download link appeared', { timeout: 60_000 });
```

- `waitFor` needs a model even under a custom executor and is never cached,
  so each run spends judgments on it. It judges again on every screen
  change, and on every location change except under `vision: 'only'`, up
  to `maxModelCalls` (25): for a long wait on a screen that keeps
  changing (a progress counter), raise `interval`. The test timeout still
  caps its `timeout`.

- `extract` takes any Standard Schema validator (zod works); the model sees
  the schema's shape, never its value rules (`min`, `max`, lengths,
  patterns), which check what it read. Data the screen does not show is
  `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` naming what was missing, never `""` or `0`; to
  accept absence, ask for it (`'the phone, or null when none is shown'`
  with `.nullable()`).

For a debug view that pairs each action with the screen it started on, give
`agent.act` an `onBeforeAction` hook that calls `app.screenshot`, and match
each capture to `onAction` by `index`, which restarts at 1 in each `act` call.
It runs before replayed actions too, does not wait for the screen to settle,
and a failed action gets a capture but no `onAction`.
Narrow `onAction`'s event on `action` for coordinates, replay included:
`point` for `tapAt`/`hoverAt`, `from`/`to` for `dragAt`. They are in the
same space as `screen.tapAt` and `boundingBox()`, rounded and clamped to the
viewport. Mobile engines have no `hoverAt` or `dragAt`.

`vision` on a judgment picks the evidence: `false` (default) the tree;
`true` the tree plus a masked screenshot; `'only'` the screenshot alone, for
what the screen presents (an overlay, a broken layout, a chart) where the
tree would answer first. `'only'` never falls back to the tree: unprovably
masked pixels fail with `POLICY_DENIED`.

### Viewport exploration

With `explore: true`, `agent.assert` can scroll the current screen and combine
evidence from several viewports. This helps when a list fits on a tablet but
needs scrolling on a phone.

```ts
await agent.assert('Settings lists HOS Settings, Account, Language and Theme', {
  explore: true,
  maxSteps: 10,
  maxModelCalls: 6,
});
```

Exploration offers `observe`, `scroll`, `scroll_to`, and project tools declared
`mutates: false`. The built-in executor also offers `screenshot` when `vision`
is `true` or `'only'`; the default is tree-only. Other actions are rejected. The viewport stays
where exploration ends.

Defaults are 10 scroll actions and 6 model calls, each capped at the selected
agent's configured limit. Overrides may exceed the 10/6 defaults, up to the
configured limits. The deadline
defaults to `judgmentTimeout`. `maxSteps` or `maxModelCalls` without
`explore: true` throws `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The built-in executor uses
`agents.<name>.model`, even when `judge` is configured.

A contradiction is `ASSERTION_FAILED`; insufficient evidence within the time
or action/model budget is `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE`.

Use `waitFor` for a condition that changes over time, and `explore` for content
elsewhere on the current screen.

## Write instructions the model can execute

- One goal per `act`; goal order is the test's, the path the model's.
- Keep each goal atomic: one outcome that one check confirms. When two
  parts of an instruction each leave a state worth checking, they are two
  goals, each its own `act`. Steps toward a single outcome
  are the path, not more goals: scrolling to a control, closing a banner,
  opening the menu that holds it, filling the fields of one form.
- A split flow fails at the goal that broke. Each goal replays from its own
  recording and gets its own `maxSteps` and `maxModelCalls`; the test
  timeout still caps them all.

```ts
// BAD: three goals in one instruction, one recording.
await agent.act('open the Pro plan, set the seats to {seats}, and check out', { params: { seats: 3 } });

// GOOD: arrange with two atomic goals, act with the one under test, assert last.
test('checks out the Pro plan', async ({ app, agent, screen }) => {
  await app.open('/plans');
  await agent.act('open the Pro plan');
  await agent.act('set the seats to {seats}', { params: { seats: 3 } });
  await agent.waitFor('the cart shows the Pro plan with 3 seats');

  await agent.act('check out');

  await expect(screen.getByText('Order confirmed')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(screen.getByText('Pro plan, 3 seats')).toBeVisible();
});
```

Choosing the seats is its own behavior, so it gets its own test that ends
after `set the seats` and asserts the seat count. Tests follow arrange, act,
assert, one behavior each (topic `writing-tests`, "Structure").

- Use the words on screen: `'open the Billing tab'`, not `'upgrade'`.
- Values go in `params`, never expanded: `act('rename to {name}', { params })`.
- Do not describe mechanics the runner handles: waiting, scrolling, retries.
- End the test with a check of the outcome. A passing locator or engine
  matcher, `agent.assert`, or wait confirms every `act` before it, which
  lets the cache record them; close an arrange block of `act` goals with a
  wait for its state, so a failure later in the test keeps them recorded:

```ts
await agent.act('create a workspace named "Atlas" on the Pro plan');

await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveText('Created "Atlas" on the Pro plan');
```

The model gets the instruction verbatim plus the params as a separate
block; the check also makes the test model-portable. Off-screen state (a
database row) can land after `act` returns; `expect.poll` the read instead
of sleeping.

## What the model sees

A redacted snapshot of the screen (roles, names, text, states), prior-step
summaries, and your context; never raw HTML, cookies, headers, environment
values, or a `Secret`'s value; password fields masked. The first
screen of a step arrives whole; later action results report what changed,
keyed by node ids stable while an element exists, or the whole screen when
most changed. Pixels arrive through `vision` on a judgment or the act loop's
`screenshot` and point tools, with secure fields masked. When
the browser engine's tree capture times out, the model gets a screenshot and
a warning, a judgment needs `vision: true`, and no control may be inferred
absent nor old node ids reused. The browser engine's tree shows a frame
from another site (a hosted card field) as its `iframe` node with none of
its content, so the agent reaches it only through pixels: script steps
there with `browser.frameLocator`, and judge it with `vision`. Nothing the
model returns runs as code or
selectors: the runner validates and authorizes every tool call first.

Project tool results and tool or engine errors are secret-redacted before the
model reads them. Text is redacted before it is cut to the output limit.

## Budgets and cost

| Call | Model calls | Default timeout |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `act` | up to `agents.<name>.maxModelCalls` (25) | the config `timeout`, 120 s |
| `assert` | 2 | 30 s |
| `extract` | 2 | 30 s |
| `waitFor` | up to `agents.<name>.maxModelCalls` (25) | 30 s |

- Slow model calls: raise the step or test `timeout` for `act`, the agent's
  `judgmentTimeout` for judgments, `actionTimeout` for slow UI.
  `STEP_TIMEOUT` and `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` fail the test; smaller goals
  help.
- `--debug` prints phase timings and a per-step table (duration, model
  calls, tokens, cache share, cost) to stderr and saves step transcripts as
  artifacts.

## The replay cache

Replay reports expose the original model as `step.cache.recordedBy` when
available; older recordings omit it. Use `--no-cache` to evaluate a new model.

A passing `agent.act` saves its actions once a later check verifies the
outcome; the next run replays them without model calls, and the live agent
continues from the current screen when the app or final state no longer
matches. Misses and hand-offs use the model; `agent.assert`,
`agent.waitFor`, and `agent.extract` are never cached.

- On by default (`read-write`), `read-only` in CI, off via `cache: 'off'`
  or `--no-cache`. Entries live in `.e2e/cache/`; deleting the directory
  only slows the next run.
- An entry is written only after a later verification passes (a locator or
  engine `expect` matcher, `locator.waitFor`, `browser.waitForURL`,
  `agent.assert`, `agent.waitFor`), so an unchecked `act` never replays; a
  plain-value `expect`, `expect.poll`, `agent.extract`, another `act`, or
  the attempt passing confirms nothing.
- A replay needs the app on the recorded route (origin, path, and query,
  ids and tokens aside; unless the recording opens with a navigation),
  re-finds each control by role, name, test id, placeholder, input purpose,
  and its named row (an unnamed control with twins and no named container
  hands off, and so does one known only by a generated test id once that id
  is gone), and passes alone only when the recorded end route is back,
  every control that appeared (with its checked or selected state) is
  there, every one that went away is gone, at least one of those changed
  during the replay, and no new alert showed; otherwise the agent takes
  over mid-step. The web engine does not observe Next.js App Router's route
  announcer, so its title echo never counts. An entry's key holds the test
  file and title path, the target, the instruction and params, the agent,
  its `context`, and the test's `agentContext`, so renaming the test or its
  file records every goal in it again, and rewording a goal records that
  goal again. `step.cache.reason` says why: `no-entry`,
  `wrong-context`, `target-not-found`, `target-ambiguous`, `end-mismatch`,
  and so on.
- A step changing nothing on screen or in the route creates no entry
  (`step.cache.write`: `no-change`) and runs live every run, strict
  included; a change only inside a frame from another site counts as
  nothing, since the tree leaves it out. A step recording no actions
  creates no entry either. A step whose
  `unique()` value equals, is spelled inside, or is the encoded form of
  another param's value is not recorded either (`step.cache.notRecorded`:
  `param-collision`).
- `e2e init` gitignores `.e2e/cache/`; remove that line to commit entries
  and share replays with CI and teammates (CI stays `read-only` unless
  `cache: 'read-write'` is set).
- A failing run keeps the entries a check confirmed before the failure. It
  evicts a replay that ran into the failure and any recording no check
  confirmed. A cancelled run and a failure where no model answered
  (`MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED`, `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`) implicate nothing and evict
  nothing.
- While you fix a test, keep the cache on: each rerun replays the goals
  whose check passed instead of calling the model for them (SKILL.md,
  "Rerunning a test while you fix it"). `--no-cache` is for ruling out a
  stale replay (topic debugging, "Tools"), and for one live run once the
  test passes.
- With committed recordings, `--strict-cache` in CI fails a recording that
  no longer replays with `REPLAY_STALE` instead of quietly spending model
  calls every run; re-record with a `read-write` run without the flag and
  with `cache.strict` off, then commit. Unrecorded steps still run live;
  retries replay too, and a strict run never writes the cache.

## Inspect what the model did

```bash
npx e2e run tests/checkout.e2e.ts --debug      # step table, transcripts as artifacts
npx e2e run tests/checkout.e2e.ts --ai-trace   # writes <output>/ai-trace.json (.e2e/ai-trace.json by default)
npx unbox-ai runs .e2e/ai-trace.json                        # one line per agent step
npx unbox-ai summary .e2e/ai-trace.json --run 0             # turns, tokens, tool calls of one step
```

Never read the trace directly: megabytes of resent context, images replaced
by byte counts. `--no-cache` traces the whole flow, since replayed steps
make no model calls. The recorder redacts serialized tool results and errors
before writing the AI trace.

## Make the agent yours

1. **The goal.** A failed step usually named something the screen does not;
   reword it with on-screen labels, and `--debug` shows what the model saw
   and tried.
2. **`context`.** Vocabulary every step needs (plan names, what a
   "workspace" is, which tab holds billing), once on `agents.<name>.context`
   or per test via `agentContext`.
3. **`system` on the agent.** How carefully it verifies, what it never
   does, how it treats a modal; a UX reviewer, a cautious QA persona, and a
   fast smoke agent are three `system` prompts on one model.
4. **Tools.** A test API the agent may call mid-flow (seed a cart, mint a
   coupon) via `tools`; see below.
5. **The model and its options.** `providerOptions` for reasoning effort,
   or another model for one persona. `--agent <name>` runs the suite as any
   configured agent, comparing candidates on the same tests; every result
   records which agent ran it.

## Beyond the built-in agent

- `tools: { seedCart }` on an agents entry adds AI SDK tools wrapped with
  `defineTool(tool({ ... }), { mutates: true })` from `e2e/agent` for a
  test API a flow calls mid-step.
- A `mutates: false` tool can call `getToolContext(options).read({ id },
  { style: ['color', 'font-weight'] })` for a node in its newest observation.
  Web reads return redacted `{ style }` under the step deadline, use no action
  slot, and never relocate stale IDs. Use `requires: ['computed-style']` to
  skip engines without support. Allowed properties and errors:
  https://e2e.com/docs/tools#read-a-nodes-computed-style.
- `createToolLoopExecutor` keeps the loop and replaces prompt and tool
  vocabulary; spread `createGrammarTools(ctx, { guard })` into its tools and
  start its `system` with `BASE_RULES` to keep the built-in actions.
- Any `StepExecutor` (`{ name, version?, cache?, runStep(ctx) }`) goes under
  `executor`; the runner still owns observations, actions, budgets, and the
  report, and `system` or `tools` beside `executor` is `INVALID_CONFIG`.

Reference: https://e2e.com/docs/agents

## In CI

Run the suite, agent steps included, on every pull request, passing the key
the config's model reads (`env: { AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }` for `gateway()`)
from secrets. Sharing `.e2e/cache/` lets CI replay verified action steps
without model calls; CI defaults (`read-only` cache, retries): topic running.

# Running a bug bash

A bug bash is many `e2e explore` runs at once, one charter each, then a
verification pass that turns every claimed bug into a repro test that fails
for the reason reported. Plan the charters, fan them out, merge the findings,
prove each bug. Report confirmed bugs only, each with its failing test.

## Contents

- 1. Prepare
- 2. Plan charters
- 3. Fan out
- 4. Merge
- 5. Triage
- 6. Verify
- 7. Report
- Rules

## 1. Prepare

- A config with a target and an agent that holds a model (topic `setup`),
  and authentication for its provider.
- The app must serve several explorers at once: start it once and set
  `reuseExisting: true` on the target's `app.command`, or declare the URL with
  port `0` so each run starts its own app on a free port. `reuseExisting` is
  ignored when `CI` is set, as in many agent sandboxes: use port `0` or
  unset `CI`. A fixed port that is not reused fails every run after the first.
- When the target's `app.command` brings up a stack of its own (a database
  it starts and removes on exit), the first explorer to finish removes the
  database under the rest. Start the stack once yourself with the config's
  command and environment, and explore with a bug-bash config that declares
  no command (below).
- Explore a production build when the project has one. A dev server that
  compiles a route on first visit reads to the explorer as a dead link.
- Seed one disposable workspace or user per charter with the project's own
  fixtures or seed scripts and declare each as a credential (`bb-<slug>`).
  Explorers that share an account report each other's edits as bugs.
- Start signed-in charters from a saved session: `e2e explore --session
  <name>` runs the setup test that saves it and explores signed in (topic
  `explore`). Each charter with its own account needs its own setup and
  session.
- Put what the local app cannot do in the agent's `context`: integrations
  without keys, what is seed data, what must never be clicked (paid runs,
  real accounts). Add the explorer's own blind spots from step 5's artifact
  bucket (the config below carries the sentence); without them those
  families dominate the findings.
- A bash against a deployed site others use is read-only: no signups,
  sign-ins, or submissions, nothing injection-shaped in URLs, no request
  loops. A WAF block is the firewall working, not a finding, and it can
  follow the runner's IP into every later charter.
- Each exploration step needs 40 or more `maxSteps` and `maxModelCalls` on
  the agent; a config tuned for test steps (`maxSteps: 15`) starves it. That
  is per step, separate from `--max-steps`, which counts a charter's steps.
- On a mobile target, declare one target per device and give each explorer
  and verifier its own (topic `setup`).
- Skip `--headed`. On an engine that records, `--video` gives each run a
  replay for any confirmed bug.

A bug-bash config, left untracked, spreads the project's config and
overrides what a bug bash needs. Typing the import as `E2EConfig` keeps
`shared.tests` and `shared.credentials` compiling when the base declares
neither:

```ts
// e2e.bugbash.config.ts
import type { E2EConfig } from 'e2e';
import { web } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { gateway } from 'ai';
import base from './e2e.config.ts';

const shared: E2EConfig = base;

// What the local app cannot do, plus the explorer's blind spots (step 5's artifact bucket).
const context =
  'Sign in with the credential the goal names. The local app sends no email and has no AI key. Never start a paid run or connect an integration. ' +
  'Not bugs: a link that opens a new tab leaves this one unchanged; accessible text splits around inline links, so judge copy by the rendered screen when a screenshot is available and never report split text alone as broken copy; an infinite-scroll "Loading more" sentinel loads when scrolled into view; images lazy-load, so scroll and wait before calling one blank.';
const persona = { model: gateway('openai/gpt-6-luna-fast'), maxSteps: 40, maxModelCalls: 40, context };

export default {
  ...shared,
  // The project's tests, so a repro can use its setup tests' sessions, plus the repro tests from step 6.
  tests: [
    ...[shared.tests ?? 'tests/**/*.e2e.ts'].flat().filter((glob) => !glob.startsWith('!tests/bugbash/')),
    'tests/bugbash/**/*.e2e.ts',
  ],
  // The app already runs: no command.
  targets: [{ name: 'web', engine: web(), app: { url: 'http://127.0.0.1:3000' } }],
  retries: 0,
  reporters: ['list'],
  credentials: {
    ...shared.credentials,
    // The seed script's password, from the environment rather than the file.
    'bb-cart': { username: 'bb-cart@example.test', password: process.env.BUGBASH_PASSWORD ?? '' },
    'bb-account': { username: 'bb-account@example.test', password: process.env.BUGBASH_PASSWORD ?? '' },
  },
  // The postures from step 2 as personas: same model and budgets, a different stance; each charter picks one with --agent (step 3).
  agents: {
    default: persona,
    skeptic: { ...persona, system: 'Distrust every number, date, count, and claim on screen; cross-check each against every other place it appears.' },
    fuzzer: { ...persona, system: "At every input, run the goal's input matrix before anything else, judging each entry before the next. Never take the happy path." },
  },
} satisfies E2EConfig;
```

Set `BUGBASH_PASSWORD` to 6 or more characters first, or the config fails to
load: a shorter password can't be redacted without rewriting ordinary text,
so an account the app seeds with one (`admin`/`admin`) needs a longer
password before it can be a credential. Pass `--config e2e.bugbash.config.ts`
to every command below, and `open_session {config: "e2e.bugbash.config.ts"}`
over MCP.

## 2. Plan charters

A charter is one `e2e explore` goal: one area, one posture, one sentence,
naming the start route and, when needed, the credential (`Sign in as
credential bb-cart. Starting at /cart, ...`). Read the routes, navigation,
and forms first; for a branch, `git diff --stat` against the base.

| Posture | Charter shape |
| --- | --- |
| First-time user | `Starting at /signup, sign up and complete onboarding like a first-time user; report anything confusing, broken, or inconsistent` |
| Numbers and copy | `Starting at /cart, change quantities and apply a coupon; check every price, total, and label against the rest of the page` |
| Edge input | `Starting at /settings/profile, submit each field empty, too long, with unicode and with leading spaces; report validation that is missing or wrong` |
| State | `Starting at /projects, create, rename, and delete a project, reloading and going back after each; report state that is lost or stale` |
| Error paths | `Starting at /login, try a wrong password, an unknown account, and a locked account; report errors that are missing, misleading, or leak detail` |

Aim for five to ten charters, each with its own slug. Overlap is fine;
duplicates merge in step 4. Give each posture its persona (config above),
picked per charter in step 3: a generic agent walks past a stat that
contradicts the same stat on another page, the skeptic catches it. An
edge-input charter names its exact matrix (empty, a 300-character string,
unicode, leading spaces, literal special characters) or it spends the whole
time budget before judging a single result.

## 3. Fan out

One `e2e explore` per charter with its own output directory:
`--output .e2e/bugbash/<slug>` writes `report.json` and `results/` there,
and `--reporter list,markdown` adds `summary.md`. `e2e init` gitignores
specific `.e2e/` paths, not `.e2e/bugbash/`: add it to `.gitignore` or
delete it when done, and delete it before a new bug bash. `charters.txt` and
the logs under it are yours; the rest is the runner's output, read only.

Run them as background shell jobs, four at a time, not as subagents. One
line per charter, `slug|target|agent|charter`, the agent naming its persona,
then (`xargs -0 -P` is a GNU and BSD extension, present on macOS and Linux):

```bash
mkdir -p .e2e/bugbash
cat > .e2e/bugbash/charters.txt <<'CHARTERS'
cart|web|skeptic|Starting at /cart, change quantities and apply a coupon; check every price, total, and label against the rest of the page
account|web|fuzzer|Starting at /settings/profile, submit each field empty, a 300-character value, unicode, and leading spaces; report validation that is missing or wrong
CHARTERS
while IFS='|' read -r slug target agent charter; do
  [ -n "$slug" ] && printf '%s\0%s\0%s\0%s\0' "$slug" "$target" "$agent" "$charter"
done < .e2e/bugbash/charters.txt | xargs -0 -n 4 -P 4 sh -c \
  'npx e2e explore "$4" --config e2e.bugbash.config.ts --target "$2" --agent "$3" --output ".e2e/bugbash/$1" --max-steps 15 --timeout 900000 --video --reporter list,markdown < /dev/null > ".e2e/bugbash/$1.log" 2>&1' _
```

`--timeout` ends a charter with its assessment whatever its step count, and
a step takes about a minute, so the flags above give each charter about
fifteen minutes. Under a time limit, size the first round to end by about a
third of it.

The log's summary prints `AI` (cost) and `Duration`. Exit code `1` means
issues were reported: read the log either way. Exit codes `2` and `3` are
setup and environment problems; fix them and rerun that charter alone.

## 4. Merge

Read each log's `Findings` section (topic `explore`); `summary.md` holds the
same, and `report.json` has the record under `run.explore`. The video is in
the attempt's `video/` directory under `.e2e/bugbash/<slug>/results/`.

Merge findings that describe one defect: same path, same broken behavior.
Keep the clearest reproduction and every charter that hit it. Keep warnings
in a separate list unless the user asked for polish.

A charter's video is not masked: check it for secrets before sharing (topic
`writing-tests`).

## 5. Triage

Sort every finding before writing any test. Read the source to sort them.

| Bucket | Sign | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Explorer artifact | A "dead" `target="_blank"` link whose destination opens when clicked with popup capture or navigated to directly, a broken sentence the screenshot renders whole, a "Loading more" sentinel nothing scrolled to, a lazy-loading image or embed | Rejected with the check that settled it; settle this bucket first. A new-tab link whose destination never opens stays a candidate |
| Environment | Fails on a key, a service, or a limit only the local stack lacks (an email provider, an AI key, a billing plan) | Rejected, naming the variable or service; note separately when the app handles the failure badly in a way production users would see, such as showing the raw error |
| Design | The code, its tests, or its copy say the behavior is intended | Rejected, citing where |
| Fixture | The seed data lacks a field real records always have | Rejected, naming the field |
| Candidate | None of the above | Verify it (step 6) |

## 6. Verify

A finding is a model's claim; prove each candidate before reporting it. When
your client can start subagents (Claude Code's Agent or Task tool, for one),
start one per area with its three to five candidates as the log printed
them and these steps, up to four at a time (the `e2e mcp` server's default
session limit, which step 4 uses). Each reports back, per finding:
confirmed or rejected, the root cause as `file:line` when it may read the
source, the repro test path, and the failure it saw. Without subagents,
verify one area after another.

1. Read `actual` against the screenshot, or the video when there is none.
   A finding the evidence contradicts is rejected here. Settle the artifact
   bucket first: a "dead" link's destination must actually open (a valid
   href with a prevented default is still dead), a copy claim must show in
   the rendered screenshot.
2. Write a repro test from the finding: its reproduction as `agent.act`
   steps and its expected behavior as the closing `agent.assert`, so it
   fails today and passes once the bug is fixed. It needs no locators. Sign
   in as the charter did, with its credential as step parameters or a setup
   test's session. Assert only the defect: a count or a record another repro
   changes makes it fail for the wrong reason. Put it under `bugbash/`
   inside the directory the config's `tests` glob covers
   (`tests/bugbash/<slug>.e2e.ts` for the default): a file the glob does not
   match is never selected, whatever path you pass to `e2e run`. Tag it
   `{ tags: ['bugbash'] }`.

   ```ts
   // tests/bugbash/cart-line-quantity.e2e.ts
   import { describe, test } from '@e2e-dev/web';
   import { credentials } from 'e2e';

   describe('cart', { tags: ['bugbash'] }, () => {
     test('a cart line totals its quantity times the unit price', async ({ app, agent }) => {
       const shopper = credentials.user('bb-cart');
       await app.open('/');
       await agent.act('sign in with the given credentials', {
         params: { username: shopper.username, password: shopper.password },
       });
       await agent.act('add "Dune" to the cart');
       await agent.waitFor('you are signed in and the cart holds "Dune"');

       await agent.act('set the quantity of "Dune" in the cart to 2');

       await agent.assert('the cart line for "Dune" totals twice its unit price');
     });
   });
   ```

   Write it in the shape topic `writing-tests` describes: arrange, closed by
   a wait for the starting state, then the one action that shows the defect,
   then the assertions. The wait keeps a broken setup from passing as the
   defect, and keeps the setup goals cached across the failing runs.
3. Run your repros with the bug-bash config and an output directory of your
   own, `npx e2e run tests/bugbash/<slug>.e2e.ts --config
   e2e.bugbash.config.ts --output .e2e/bugbash/verify-<area>` (a run clears
   its output's results, and another subagent may be reading them), then one
   file alone while you fix it. Confirmed when it fails on the
   reported defect: `ASSERTION_FAILED` from the closing `assert`, or a
   failed `act` whose message names the defect. A failed `act` carries the
   code the model chose, so only its message and screenshot tell the defect
   apart from a failure short of it. A blocked `act`, a timeout, a setup
   error, a failed arrange wait, or a failure that names something else means the repro is wrong:
   sharpen the step and rerun. A passing test means the bug did not
   reproduce: reject the finding, say so, and move the test out of
   `tests/bugbash/` (to `.e2e/bugbash/extra-tests/`, or offer it as a
   regression test). Only failing repro tests stay there.
4. When the user wants a scripted regression test, harden a confirmed repro
   with `screen` actions and exact `expect` values (topic `writing-tests`):
   with the `e2e mcp` server registered, `open_session` with the bug-bash
   config, pass its session id to every call, walk the reproduction, and
   `locate` each locator before writing it (topic `mcp`). Close your session
   when done. A scripted step that opens a native dialog needs
   `browser.onDialog` first.

## 7. Report

Run every repro once, `npx e2e run --tag bugbash --config
e2e.bugbash.config.ts`, so each bug you report still fails. Lead with the confirmed bugs, most severe first. For each: title, path, one
line of expected against actual, root cause when known, steps, screenshot
and video paths, repro test, and the charters that found it. Then the
environment candidates that are production risks, marked unverified. Then
the rejected findings grouped by reason (environment, design, fixture, did
not reproduce), and the warnings. End with the charters run, their cost, and
the areas no charter reached.

The repro tests fail until the bugs are fixed: where the project's `tests`
glob covers `tests/bugbash/`, its gating run leaves them out
(`npx e2e run --exclude-tag bugbash`) or they stay uncommitted. Offer to fix
each bug: the repro test turning green is the proof, and it stays as the
regression test with its `bugbash` tag removed.

## Rules

- Never report an unverified finding as a bug. "The explorer reported" is
  not "confirmed".
- Under a time limit, spend it: once a round is verified, run charters for
  the areas and postures no charter reached, until about a tenth of the
  time is left. Report each bug as soon as its repro confirms it, so a bash
  cut off at the limit keeps it.
- One charter, one area. A charter that spans the whole app ends at its
  step budget having skimmed everything.
- Seeded data and test accounts the app ships for development are not
  bugs; say so in the agent's `context`.
- Leave the project's files as you found them: the bug-bash config, seed
  script, and repro tests stay untracked until the user asks otherwise, and
  stop the stack you started when the user is done.
