# Debugging a failing run

Paths below sit under the configured `output` directory; `.e2e` is the
default.

## Contents

- Read the failure
- Error codes
- Tools
- Flaky tests
- Is it the app?

## Read the failure

1. Every failure in the `list` output names the failing line with a code
   frame, where the screen was (`❯ at`: a URL on the web, the app and
   screen title on a device), the nodes nearest a failed locator
   (`❯ on screen`), and ends with `❯ trace
   .e2e/results/<test>/trace.md`. Open that trace page: `Look at:` (the line it unwound
   through), `Expected:` / `Observed:` (an `expect`), `Asked for:` and
   `Waited:` (a locator), whether every attempt failed alike (a bug, not a
   flake), then every step with what it did under it:
   - the node an action landed on (`tap button "Save" (12ms)`), or `✗` and
     its code;
   - what an assertion read while it waited (`expect gave up after 16 reads
     in 1.6s: text "0 remaining" (1 match) x16`); one value throughout
     points at a wrong expectation, a broken app, or one slower than the
     timeout, changing values at a race;
   - what the app logged meanwhile (`✗ network error: POST /api/save 500`,
     `✗ uncaught error: ...`, `⚠ console warning: ...`, `ℹ console: ...`);
     `❯ app 2 errors` in the terminal quotes the first 3 errors, and the page's
     `## App log` lists up to 50 with their step, errors and warnings
     first, counting the rest;
   - where the page went (`↪ navigated to /login`, a new tab the app
     opened, a frame that loaded);
   - how the screen changed since the step before (`screen: 2 changes since
     step 3` with the added, removed, and changed nodes); `unchanged` after
     an action means it had no visible effect;
   - the cache's decision for an agent step: replayed, handed off and where
     (`at action 2 of 3, tap button "Apply": ...`), what became of the
     recording, and the entry file;
   - the agent's last turns, loop-guard notes included, and under
     `## Screen at failure` the nodes closest to what a failed locator
     asked for and the screen, one node per line.
   `trace` (default `retain-on-failure`) chooses which tests keep a page;
   `--trace` keeps one for every test of a run.
2. Fix from that evidence, never by walking the flow again from the start
   over MCP: the run already saw every screen up to the failure.
   - Fix every line it covers, not only the failing one. `observed` is what
     the screen showed; a `❯ on screen` node is most likely what a failed
     locator meant; the screen at failure (also `screen-at-failure.txt`,
     item 5) holds the names the rest of that screen's lines need.
   - A test stops at its first failed step (an `expect.soft` lets it go
     on), and every wrong line after it costs another run. Before
     rerunning, check the lines after it as far as you can: against the
     screen at failure, the app source, or a live session.
   - For a screen the evidence and the source leave out, look live (topic
     `mcp`): open or reuse a session, go straight to that screen, then
     `observe` and `locate`, or `run_code` for the fixed line and the ones
     after it. On the web, `navigate` to the path of the `❯ at` URL or the
     screen's route, and tap only to reach a state no URL opens. A device
     session starts on the app's launch screen: take the shortest path from
     there.
   - Then rerun only that test by `file:line` (SKILL.md, "Rerunning a
     test while you fix it"; topic `mcp` says when a session must close
     first).
3. `.e2e/report.json` holds the same facts for scripts, not for reading:
   each step's `events` (`engine`, `poll`, `navigation`) and the attempt's
   `appLog` (each line's `step` is a step `index`) are what the page's step
   lines are rendered from, before it filters and caps them.
4. When a script needs them:

```bash
jq '.run | {status, exitCode, errors}' .e2e/report.json
jq '.run.results[] | select(.selected and .status != "passed") | {titlePath, file, status}' .e2e/report.json
jq '.run.results[] | select(.selected and .status != "passed") | .attempts[-1]
    | {status, error, failure, steps: [.steps[] | select(.status != "passed") | {api, label, source, status, error}], artifacts}' .e2e/report.json
```

   `error.details` holds the facts, `error.source` the line, `failure` the
   `url`, `screen` and `screenshot` artifact ids, and `candidates`; a
   failed agent step has `turns`; any agent step has
   `observationTruncated: true` when a semantic observation was incomplete;
   `selected` drops filtered-out tests
   (recorded as `skipped`).
5. Artifacts, under `.e2e/results/<test>/attempt-<n>/` (`rerun-<n>/attempt-<m>/`
   for a `--last-failed` rerun), beside the
   trace page: `screen-at-failure.txt`
   and the engine's screenshot per failed attempt; downloads; with
   `--video` the recording (`video/video.webm` in a local browser, each
   later page `video/video-part<n>.webm` with its own `startedAt`;
   `video/video.mp4` on a device; a provider's file or link); with
   `--debug` every agent step's transcript.

## Error codes

| Code | Usual cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED` | The config throws while loading (a refused engine option is `INVALID_CONFIG` instead) or imports a missing package, subpath, or removed export such as `defineConfig` | Install the dependency, or fix the import or line quoted |
| `INVALID_CONFIG`, `INVALID_GLOB` | Unknown or foreign key (`app`, `webServer`, `use`, `projects`, `baseURL`), `json` with `list`; a `tests` glob with braces, classes, an absolute path, or no wildcard | The message names the key or glob to write; the app is declared in the target's `app` |
| `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` | Wrong `--config` path, or an MCP `open_session` in a directory with no config | Fix the path; in a directory with no config, pass `engine` to `open_session` (topic `mcp`) |
| `CONFIG_AMBIGUOUS` | Both `.ts` and `.mts` present | Keep one |
| `ENGINE_NOT_INSTALLED` | An MCP `open_session {engine}` named a package that is not in the project, beside e2e, or in `~/.e2e/engines` | Run the install command the message names |
| `NO_TESTS` | The glob, a positional, or a filter matched nothing; the message names each empty positional and each undeclared `--tag` with the nearest declared one | Check the config `tests`, the file suffix (`.e2e.ts` by default), the tag names |
| `NO_LAST_RUN` | `--last-failed` found no `.e2e/report.json` | Run once without it |
| `INVALID_CHANGED_SINCE` | `--changed-since` names no commit in the checkout, shares no history with HEAD (a shallow clone, or unrelated histories), or git is missing | Run from a git checkout with git installed; check the ref; fetch it and more history (`git fetch --unshallow`, or `fetch-depth: 0` on `actions/checkout`); for unrelated histories, name a ref on HEAD's history |
| `COLLECTION_ERROR` | `async` describe body, `test.setup` inside `describe`, an option forbidden in a serial group, registration outside collection | Restructure per `writing-tests` |
| `HOOK_FAILED` | `beforeAll` or `afterAll` threw; its scope's tests skip | Fix the hook; the report carries its error |
| `UNSUPPORTED_ARTIFACT` | A test's or target's `video` on an engine that cannot record | Drop it there, or set it at the config root or CLI (such targets skip with a notice) |
| `BROWSER_INSTALL_FAILED`, `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT` | Browser download failed; engine init or attempt start exceeded `launchTimeout` | Run the quoted `npx @e2e-dev/web install <names>` or `pnpm exec e2e-web install <names>` (`--with-deps` on bare Linux); raise the root `launchTimeout` (60 s default) |
| `APP_UNREACHABLE` | The app failed readiness or its command exited. An exit after readiness stops only dependent targets with unfinished work. On a device, the message can identify a failed iOS automation runner | Read the exit details and any log excerpt. Set `app.command.log` if requested. Check `app.url`, the port, and the command settings. Runner: rerun, else `npx agent-device daemon stop` and reboot the simulator |
| `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING` | Something already serves `url` when `command` should start, such as the app an open `e2e mcp` session started | A session's app: `close_session` before the run (topic `mcp`). Otherwise stop it if you started it, else offer the user `reuseExisting: true` (CI ignores it) |
| `APP_URL_REQUIRED`, `APP_NOT_OPEN` | A navigation on a target without `app.url`; a `screen` call before `app.open()` | Add `app.url` to the target; open the app first |
| `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `INVALID_LOCATOR` | A step argument failed validation; a locator got a bad option or filter key | Fix the call the code frame names |
| `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` | Wrong role or name, inexact text, element off screen or in an iframe, page not open | Read the markup for the accessible name; `exact: false` or a RegExp; `browser.frameLocator` for iframes; `app.open()` first; `--headed` |
| `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` | Two matches (hidden duplicate, repeated label) | `{ name }`, a container scope, `filter`, `first()`, or `{ visible: true }` |
| `ASSERTION_FAILED` | Wrong expectation, or the state settles later than 5 s; for `agent.assert`, a false judgment (explained in the report) | Compare with the report's actual text or the screenshot; `{ timeout }` on the matcher; rewrite the question |
| `ASSERTION_INCONCLUSIVE` | `agent.assert` or `agent.extract` asked about what the screen does not show (another page, still loading, only in pixels, inside a frame from another site); a failure, never a pass | `app.open()` or `agent.waitFor` the right screen first; ask about what is shown; `vision: true` when the answer is in pixels (the message says so) |
| `MODEL_OUTPUT_INVALID` | An `extract` or `assert` answer failed the schema after one repair round | Simplify the schema or question; pick a stronger model |
| `ACTION_FAILED` | Element not actionable (covered, disabled, detached), or an operation timed out | `waitFor` the condition right before the action that failed; close overlays; check `actionTimeout` |
| `TEST_TIMEOUT` | The attempt exceeded `timeout` (120 s) | Split the test, or raise `timeout` |
| `STEP_NOT_AWAITED` | The body returned while a step or `expect.poll` still ran, or an `afterEach` hook or fixture teardown returned while an `expect.poll` still ran: a call without `await` | `await` the call the code frame names (every `app`, `agent`, `screen`, `expect`, `expect.poll` call) |
| `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` | `agents.<name>.model` holds no AI SDK instance: reported once under `run.errors` at the first `agent` fixture; the run stops. A model-less custom executor fails only `waitFor` and `extract` this way. Also GitHub Copilot refusing the configured model to the account (`model_not_supported`, a plan or settings limit the listing cannot show): reported once at the first call, the run stops | Construct one, e.g. `gateway('openai/gpt-6-luna-fast')` from `ai`, and export its key (`AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`); for Copilot, pick an id the plan serves |
| `MODEL_PROVIDER_FAILED` | Network, 5xx, rate limit, no credits, or no response in 120 s, after the transport retries | Check the credential (the key; for keyless `gateway()` the Vercel CLI login and `.vercel/project.json`) and quota; retry (exit 3) |
| `MODEL_REFUSED` | The model refused the prompt (finish reason `content-filter`). Exit 1 | Rephrase the prompt or instruction, or switch to a different model |
| `REPLAY_STALE` | `--strict-cache` or `cache.strict`, and a committed recording no longer replays; `step.cache.reason` says why | Rerun read-write with the knob the message names off; commit the changed entry under the directory it names (a custom `cache.store` is written by that run) |
| `AUTOMATION_UNSUPPORTED` | The step needs an interaction the engine's toolset lacks (a right-click on a device, say); blocked, exit 1 | Reach the result another way the engine supports (a long press, a menu button), or run the test on a target that supports it |
| `STEP_TIMEOUT`, `STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` | Goal too big or ambiguous, or a slow provider | Split the goal, use on-screen wording, add vocabulary via `agents.<name>.context` or `agentContext`; raise `maxSteps` or `maxModelCalls` (budget), the config `timeout` (`act`), `judgmentTimeout` (judgments); `--debug` |
| `CONTEXT_OVERFLOW` | Screen plus step history did not fit the model's context window (`act` after one shrink-and-retry; a judgment on the first overflow) | Lower `agents.<name>.maxObservationBytes`, split the step, or pick a larger-window model |
| `POLICY_DENIED` | A URL whose scheme is not `http:` or `https:` (`file:`, `view-source:`, `data:`); a password `Secret` into a non-password sink; reading a secure field, `toHaveValue`, `toHaveText`, `toContainText`, `toHaveAttribute` included; `vision: 'only'` with pixels withheld | http(s) or `about:blank` only; passwords into password inputs only; assert the outcome, not the value |
| `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY` | A fixture the engine lacks (`browser` on a device), `schema` or `vision` on `act`, an action the surface lacks | Declare `requires: ['browser']`; drop the option or action |
| `SESSION_UNAVAILABLE`, `SESSION_CONTRACT` | `session: 'x'` with no setup saving `x`; a setup that skipped a declared name. `SESSION_MISMATCH`, `SESSION_EXPIRED`, `SESSION_INVALID`: the stored session is another run's or app's, expired, or corrupt | Add or fix the `test.setup`; rerun it |
| `ONLY_IN_CI` | `test.only` reached CI | Remove it |
| `AUTH_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE`, `AUTH_CREDENTIAL_INVALID` | `credentials.user('x')` for an undeclared name; the app rejected a configured credential | Add it to `config.credentials`; fix the stored value |
| `SECRET_UNAVAILABLE` | `secrets.get('x')` for an undeclared name | Add it to `config.secrets`; `E2E_SECRET_X` only overrides a declared one |

## Tools

| Do | When |
| --- | --- |
| `--headed` | Watch the failing step |
| `--step --headed` | A person steps through the test one key per step |
| `--step`, then `e2e run --step next` | An agent steps through the test: each command prints how the step it ran ended and returns at the next held step with the screen it waits on; `stop` ends the run |
| `--workers 1 --retries 0` | Take parallelism and retries out of the picture |
| `--action-timeout 5000` | While writing a test: a wrong locator fails in 5 s instead of 30 s (`--assertion-timeout` for `expect`). Keep it longer than the slowest screen takes to load |
| `--no-cache` | Rule out a stale `agent.act` replay; one run, not every rerun. A failed run already deletes the replay that ran into the failure, so rerun with the cache on first. When the failure repeats after a replay the trace page shows as kept and the `--no-cache` run passes, tighten the next check or wait after that goal (the arrange block's closing wait, or the assertions): the stale replay then fails it and is deleted |
| `--debug` | Each agent step's duration, model calls, cost, transcript |
| `--ai-trace`, then `npx unbox-ai runs .e2e/ai-trace.json` | What the model saw and called |
| `--video`, `--video=retain-on-failure` | Watch the failed attempt; `step.startedAt` minus the segment's `startedAt` is the step's offset into it |
| `command.log: '.e2e/logs/app.log'` | The app's output when it never gets ready or errors mid-test |
| `await app.screenshot('before-submit')` | Evidence at a point you choose; it masks secure fields only |
| `app.startRecording()`, then `await app.stopRecording()` | One transition as a video; fails while the test's `video` records |
| `CI=1 npx e2e run` | Reproduce CI-only behaviour (defaults: topic running) |

## Flaky tests

- A read (`textContent()`, `count()`) caught a value mid-update: use a
  matcher.
- Shared data: unique names per run, `afterEach` cleanup, or a `serial`
  group.
- App not ready: assert on the element you are about to use, not the
  previous page.
- An agent judgment asserts exact phrasing: judge the fact, add a
  deterministic `expect` beside it.
- Load timing: `retries` masks it; `--workers 1 --headed` shows it.
- Measure a fix: `npx e2e run <file> --repeat-each 10 --retries 0`
  (`--no-cache` for agent steps). `Repeats` reads `0 of 1 test passed all
  10 runs` over `3/10 passed · repeat 0 ASSERTION_FAILED · ...` (0-based)
  before, `1 of 1 test passed all 10 runs` after.

## Is it the app?

A deterministic step failing every run at the same place with the same code
is a product bug or a changed screen, not a flake: reproduce once with
`--headed`, then fix the app or update locator and expectation together. A
blocked agent step (`AUTH_CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE`, `ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE`,
`SEED_DATA_MISSING`) exits 2 or 3 on purpose: fix the environment.

# Exploring without a test

`e2e explore` runs the agent against the app with a goal instead of a test
file: see what it can do with an app before tests exist, hunt for regressions
on a branch, or find what is worth turning into a test. It needs a config with
a target and an agent that holds a model, nothing else. With no config, it
runs the `e2e init` wizard first in a terminal; without one (an agent's
shell, CI) it fails with `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`, so run `npx e2e init --yes` first.

```bash
npx e2e explore   # goal: "Explore the app and find bugs"
npx e2e explore 'Explore checkout like a first-time buyer and report anything off'
npx e2e explore --target web --max-steps 4 --headed
npx e2e explore 'Hunt for broken forms' --video
npx e2e explore --session admin 'Explore the admin settings'
npx e2e explore --changed-since origin/main   # explore what the branch changed
```

## Contents

- What a run does
- Start signed in
- Flags
- Reading the result
- When it does not fit

## What a run does

1. Opens the app: the target's URL, or on a device the pinned app, launched
   fresh. Explore installs no build, so a local device target needs
   `app.bundleId`; an `appPath` alone leaves nothing to launch.
2. Plans one step: a structured model call reads the goal, the steps and
   findings so far, and the current screen, and answers with a title and a
   concrete charter for one flow, or decides the goal is covered.
3. Runs the charter as an `agent.act()` step with the project's tools plus
   `report_finding`. The agent reports each defect the moment it has evidence:
   title, `issue` or `warning`, severity 1 to 5, expected, actual, reproduction
   steps. The runner adds the path and a redacted screenshot.
4. Repeats until the planner finishes, the step limit, the clock, or three
   failed or blocked steps in a row that reported nothing; then asks for a
   closing assessment.

A failed step does not end the run: it is recorded, and only reported issues
fail the product verdict. A run whose charters were all blocked stays blocked.
A step that hits its action or time budget ended at its limit and counts as
neither. Configured `credentials` reach the explorer as step secrets: the
planner knows the account names and usernames, and the agent fills passwords
with `type_secret` by name. That tool is offered only when the engine can fill
secrets; otherwise the agent skips signing in and says so in the step summary.

## Start signed in

`--session <name>` starts from a session a setup test saves
(`test.setup('...', { sessions: ['admin'] }, ...)` and `session.save('admin')`,
topic `writing-tests`). The run collects the config's test files, runs exactly
the setup that declares the session, then restores it into the exploration
and opens the app, as a test with
`{ session: 'admin' }` does. No other test runs. The setup runs as for
`e2e run`, with the configured agents, cache, and retries; only the
exploration runs as the explorer. The planner and the agent are told they
start signed in, so no charter is spent signing in again. A name no setup
declares fails before any app process starts with `COLLECTION_ERROR`, naming
the declared sessions.

Findings keep their screenshots after a setup that filled a secret. Only
configured secrets are redacted (topic `writing-tests`).

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[goal]` | `Explore the app and find bugs` | One quoted sentence: the area and the posture. |
| `--target <id>` | first configured target | The one target to explore. |
| `--agent <name>` | `default` | Build the explorer from another configured agent (`agents.<name>`). |
| `--session <name>` | none | Run the setup that saves this session, then explore with it restored. |
| `--changed-since <ref>` | none | Explore what the branch changed since the merge base of the ref and HEAD. The planner reads the commit messages and the committed diff, and plans charters for the screens the change can affect. Only a defect the change can cause is an `issue`; one elsewhere is a `warning`. With no goal, the goal becomes `Explore what this change affects and find bugs in it`, and the planner may skip a change no user can see, such as docs or tests only. That run ends `skipped` and passes. In CI it needs the base in the checkout (`fetch-depth: 0`), and a clean working tree for the skip. |
| `--max-steps <n>` | 8 (1 to 100) | Exploration steps at most. |
| `--timeout <ms>` | 600000 (180000 to 7200000) | Wall clock; the last minute is for the assessment. |
| `--headed`, `--reporter`, `--output`, `--debug`, `--ai-trace`, `--trace [mode]`, `--video [mode]` | as `run` | Same meaning as for `e2e run`. The exploration is one attempt, so a retry mode (`on-first-retry`, `on-all-retries`) records nothing (the run's notice says to pass `--trace on`); put the goal before a bare `--trace` or `--video`. |

Per-step action and model-call budgets default to 40 each;
`agents.<name>.maxSteps` and `agents.<name>.maxModelCalls` in the config
override them. The replay cache is off and retries are zero for the
exploration.

## Reading the result

Exit code `0`: steps ran, no `issue` was reported, and not every charter was
blocked; warnings are allowed. With `--changed-since`, a change the planner
skipped before the first step (no file a user can see) is also `0`. Exit
code `1`: at least one `issue`, or no step ran and nothing was found. If every charter was blocked and no `issue` was
reported, the run is `blocked` even with warnings, and the exit code is the
first blocker's own, as for `run`: 1 for an automation limit, 2 for a missing
model, credentials, seed data, or test setup, 3 for an unavailable
environment. When a charter passes, fails, or exhausts its budget, reported
issues decide the verdict. Other errors use `2` and `3` as for `run`.

The terminal shows each step by its title with its duration, actions, and
findings, and each finding the moment it is reported as
`⚑ high issue  Title (/path)`. At the end a `Findings` section lists every
finding, issues first and the most severe first, each with where it was seen,
its screenshot path, expected against actual, and the steps that reach it;
then the `Assessment` and the `run` summary with `Findings` and `Steps` in
place of `Test Files` and `Tests`. Severity words: critical 5, high 4,
medium 3, low 2, trivial 1. `.e2e/report.json` has the record under
`run.explore`:

```json
{
  "goal": "...",
  "budgets": { "maxSteps": 8, "timeoutMs": 600000 },
  "ended": "finished | skipped | step-limit | time | stuck | aborted",
  "summary": "the closing assessment",
  "change": { "base": "<merge base sha>", "files": 3 },
  "steps": [{ "index": 1, "title": "...", "instruction": "...", "status": "passed | failed | blocked | exhausted", "summary": "...", "errorCode": "...", "startedAt": "...", "durationMs": 0 }],
  "findings": [{ "id": "<uuid>", "index": 0, "step": 1, "kind": "issue", "severity": 4, "title": "...", "expected": "...", "actual": "...", "reproduction": ["..."], "path": "/cart", "observationRevision": "...", "artifactId": "<attempt id>:artifact:2", "reportedAt": "..." }]
}
```

`change` is there only with `--changed-since`. A step carries `errorCode` only when it did not pass; a finding carries
`step`, `path`, `observationRevision`, and `artifactId` only when known.
`artifactId` names the evidence screenshot among the attempt's `artifacts` in
the result whose `file` is `explore`, where its path, size, and digest are.
With `--session`, `run.results` also holds the setup's result and the
project's other tests as skipped (`filtered`). The attempt directory is
`.e2e/results/explore-<slug>-<id>/attempt-1/`: the slug is the goal's first
words in lowercase ASCII, capped, and the id keeps distinct goals, targets, and
agents apart while the same goal on the same target and agent always maps to
the same directory. For example
`.e2e/results/explore-check-the-cart-totals-1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b/attempt-1/finding-1.png`.

Turn a finding into a test: its `reproduction` steps are the `agent.act()`
instructions or `screen.*` actions, and `expected` is the assertion.

## When it does not fit

The agents entry's `tools` and `system` carry over to the explorer; a
hand-rolled `StepExecutor` under `executor` is replaced by the built-in agent
for the run, with a notice on stderr, and needs a `model` on the entry (or the
executor's) or explore fails before it starts. Findings are the model's claims
plus evidence, not verified reproductions: read `actual` against the
screenshot before filing a bug.

# Driving the app over MCP

`e2e mcp` serves a project's live app to a coding agent over MCP (stdio). The
coding agent drives the app the way the testing agent does, writes a test
as it walks the flow, and checks its locators and runs its lines before
writing them. `run_tests` runs a test file or the whole suite as
`npx e2e run` does and returns what it printed (topics `running` and
`debugging`); to fix one failing test, a session can run it and stop on the
screen where it failed.

## Contents

- Setup
- Tools
- Workflow
- Fixing a failing test
- Rules

## Setup

The server ships with the project's `e2e` dependency. The e2e plugin for
Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor registers it too, as `npx -y e2e@<version> mcp`, pinned to the plugin's release (it runs that release even when the project has another e2e version); with
the plugin installed there is nothing to add. Otherwise `e2e init` offers to register it for Claude Code,
Cursor, and Codex. Reuse an existing registration; when adding one, use the project's
config so it starts in the project it drives. Install dependencies and start
the MCP client in that directory so `npx` uses the installed e2e version. In a
Bun project, use `bunx` wherever this file says `npx`.

For an existing setup, `e2e init --yes --skills none --mcp .codex/config.toml` adds Codex.
Codex reads `.codex/config.toml` in a trusted project:

```toml
[mcp_servers.e2e]
command = "npx"
args = ["e2e", "mcp"]
```

`codex mcp list`, run in the project, shows the server. Start a new session
after registering it so the tools load. Claude Code can register it with:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope project e2e -- npx e2e mcp
```

Or declare it in the client's project config (`.mcp.json` for Claude Code,
`.cursor/mcp.json` for Cursor, `.vscode/mcp.json` for VS Code):

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "e2e": { "command": "npx", "args": ["e2e", "mcp"] } } }
```

Sessions run on the project's config (`e2e.config.ts`, `.mts`, `.js`, or `.mjs`).
In a directory without one, plain `open_session` fails with `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND`.
To look at an app there anyway, name the engine package:
`open_session {engine: "@e2e-dev/web", app: {url: "http://localhost:3000"}}`, or
`{engine: {package: "@e2e-dev/mobile", options: {platform: "ios"}}, app: {bundleId: "<app>"}}`.
`engine` is the factory call a config would write: a package name calls its
default export, and `{package, export?, options?}` names another export and
passes options. An option value of that same shape is called first, which
gives an engine a device or browser provider:
`options: {platform: "ios", device: {package: "@e2e-dev/limrun", export: "limrun"}}`
is `mobile({ platform: 'ios', device: limrun() })`. That session has one
target, no credentials, secrets, or project tools, and `engine` excludes
`target`, `config`, and `test`. `ENGINE_NOT_INSTALLED` names the command that installs the package
into `~/.e2e/engines`: run it, then open again. When you cannot run it, because
the sandbox has no network or cannot write there, ask the user to run it or to
allow it, and wait. `run_tests` and
`open_session {test}` still need a config, so set the project up before
writing tests (topic `setup`). No model is needed: without the optional `ai` package, sessions
open and the deterministic tools work. A test a session runs needs one only for
an agent step with no recording.

Flags: `--config <path>` names the default config file, `--target <name>`
fixes the target every session opens on, `--headed` shows the browser or
simulator when the engine supports it in sessions that do not set `headed`
(sessions are headless by default, as in `e2e run`), `--max-sessions <n>`
sets how many sessions may be open at once (default 4, 1 through 16; one on Bun).

## Tools

Five tools, all on the server registered as `e2e`; everything a session can
do is a catalog behind `call`. Clients show them with the server name, such
as `mcp__e2e__open_session` in Claude Code (`mcp__plugin_e2e_e2e__open_session`
from the plugin); when another MCP server offers a
tool with the same name, use the `e2e` server's.

| Tool | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `open_session` | Loads the config (`config` names another file; default the nearest `e2e.config.ts`), starts the declared app command if any, boots the engine, opens the app (its URL, or launches a device's pinned app; it installs no build, so a local device needs `app.bundleId`), and returns the session id, the catalog, and the first observation. Its summary names the app URL, a port assigned for `:0`, and the app command's readiness URL and `env` names; e2e starts nothing else, so a database the app uses runs outside it. The config reads the MCP server's environment, not your shell's. `target` is required when the config declares several. `headed: true` shows the browser or simulator when the user wants to watch; without it the session follows the server's `--headed`, headless by default. `test` runs one test first and leaves the session on the screen where it stopped (see Fixing a failing test). In a directory with no config, `engine` names the engine to open on, as a package name or `{package, export?, options?}`, with `app` for the app under test (Setup); it excludes `target`, `config`, and `test`. Each session has its own browser or device. |
| `tools` | The catalog: one line per tool with its argument names (`?` marks optional), the first sentence of its description, and `[read-only]` where it changes nothing. `tools {tool}` shows the full description and the JSON Schema of its arguments. |
| `call` | Runs one catalog tool: `call {tool: "tap", args: {target: "n42"}}`. Arguments are checked against the tool's schema first; a wrong one fails with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the field. |
| `close_session` | Saves a recording still running, ends the attempt, disposes the engine, stops the app processes the session started once no other session uses them. |
| `run_tests` | Runs `e2e run` in its own process and returns its output: the command, the exit code, each test, the failure blocks, the summary. `files` takes `e2e run` positionals (`tests/checkout.e2e.ts:12`, a file, a directory, a glob); without it, every test runs. The other fields are `e2e run` flags in camelCase: `config`, `target`, `grep`, `grepInvert`, `tag`, `excludeTag`, `lastFailed`, `changedSince`, `headed`, `workers`, `retries`, `repeatEach`, `maxFailures`, `actionTimeout`, `noCache`, `updateSnapshots` (while fixing a test: `retries: 0, actionTimeout: 5000`). Needs no session. One run at a time (`RUNNER_BUSY`); cancelling the call interrupts the run. Exit 1 (a test failed) is a normal result; exit 2 and above is an error result. Output past 60,000 characters keeps its end; `.e2e/report.json` has every result. |

The catalog, per session:

| Catalog tool | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `observe` | A fresh observation: one node per line as `#id role "name" ...`, plus the current path. On the web engine a link's `href` is its path on the app URL's origin, else origin and path (`mailto:` and `tel:` keep their scheme, `blob:` its inner origin and path); `?…` and `#…` mark a dropped query or fragment, `data:…` and `javascript:…` an inline payload, a trailing `…` a target cut at 256 characters. |
| `tap`, `double_tap`, `long_press`, `right_click`, `hover`, `type`, `press`, `select`, `check`, `scroll`, `scroll_to`, `drag`, `upload`, `navigate`, `back`, `resize_viewport`, `switch_tab`, `close_tab`, `dismiss_keyboard` | The grammar verbs, as the testing agent gets them: `check` takes `checked`, `drag` a `to` node, `switch_tab` and `close_tab` a `tab` number counted from 1 in the order the tabs opened, `upload` project-relative `files` or `sample:` files (no test line for those); `dismiss_keyboard` comes with device engines. On an engine that declares `tapModifiers`, `tap`, `double_tap`, and `right_click` take an optional `modifiers` list (`Shift`, `Control`, `Alt`, `Meta`, `ControlOrMeta`) to hold keys for the click. Each reports what changed on screen and, after its lead, the test line that repeats it (`Test line: await screen.getByRole("button", "Save").tap();`) or `No test line:` and why; `observe` shows the whole screen. A verb the engine cannot honor is not listed and fails with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. |
| `type_secret` | Fills a configured secret by name: a credential's password into a password field, a `secrets` entry into any editable input; the plaintext never reaches the agent, and its test line names the credential or secret (`fill(credentials.user(name).password)`, `fill(secrets.get(name))`). Listed when the config declares `credentials` or `secrets` and the engine can fill secrets. |
| `locate` | Tries a semantic locator with exactly one of `role`, `text`, `label`, `placeholder`, `testId` (`name` only with `role`; `exact` optional; anything else is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`) and returns how many nodes match, which, and the `screen.*` call to write. |
| `run_code` | Runs test statements (`code`, as a test body writes them) on the session's `screen` and `app` with a test's waits, exactly-one rule, and matchers. Stops at the first failure and returns each statement's pass, failure (code and message), or read value, then what changed on screen. Each statement waits at most `timeout` ms (default 5000), but `timeout` doesn't stop a regex mid-match: avoid nested quantifiers such as `(\w+\s?)*`. The code is parsed, never evaluated as JavaScript: statements start with `screen`, `app`, or `expect(locator)`; arguments are literals, regexes, arrays, objects, locators, and `credentials.user(name).username`. A secret (`credentials.user(name).password`, `secrets.get(name)`) goes only into `fill`, under `type_secret`'s checks. Engine fixtures (`browser`, `device`), `app.screenshot`, and `toHaveScreenshot` are left out. Anything else is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` quoting the refused code with its line and column, and nothing runs. Reads and matchers see `<secret:name>` where a secret value is. When the config declares a secret or credential, a locator found by part of a text (a regex, an `exact` other than `true`, `hasText`) is `POLICY_DENIED` before anything runs: find it by its exact text. A matcher that expects `<secret:name>` is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The statements that pass, except reads, join `test_lines` as written. |
| `test_lines` | Every test line the session's actions printed and every statement `run_code` passed, in order, as a draft test body, starting with `await app.open();` for the session's own opening (after `open_session {test}`, the lines that continue that test, with no opening); an action without a line shows as a `//` comment. A line's locator matched the target alone on the live screen before the action (role and name first, test id last, narrowed to `{ visible: true }`, a container, or `.nth(i)` with a comment when twins share it); a fill names `credentials.user(name)` or `secrets.get(name)`, never a value; a navigation on the app's origin is written as its path. |
| `screenshot` | The masked pixels as an image. With `path` (a `.png` inside the project, relative to its root, not hidden or under a hidden directory), also saves a full-resolution masked capture there and returns its absolute path. |
| `tap_at` | Taps a point (`x`, `y` in the latest screenshot's pixels) where you aim. An engine without a bare-point tap taps the listed control under it by id instead, and fails on a point on nothing listed. Listed when the engine declares `tap` or a bare-point tap. |
| `hover_at` | Hovers a point the same way: the bare point, otherwise a listed control under it by id. Listed when the engine declares `hover` or a bare-point hover. |
| `drag_at` | Drags from one point (`x`, `y`) to another (`to_x`, `to_y`) where you aim. An engine without a bare-point drag drags by id instead when the points land on two different listed controls, and fails otherwise. Listed when the engine declares `dragTo` or a bare-point drag. |
| `type_at` | Types `value` into the field at a point: a listed input under it is filled by id; with a keyboard, anything else is tapped to focus it and typed into, at the caret unless `replace` is set. Without a keyboard a point on nothing listed fails. Listed when the engine declares `type` or a keyboard. |
| `press_at` | Sends one `key` (`Enter`, `Escape`, `Tab`) to the control at a point: a listed control gets it by id; with a keyboard, anything else is tapped to focus it and the key goes through the keyboard. Listed when the engine declares `press` or a keyboard. |
| `select_at` | Picks the option whose visible label is `value` in the select-like control at a point; the point must land on a listed select. Listed when the engine declares `select`. |
| `start_recording` | Starts a video of the app (`name` optional, for the file name). Listed when the engine records video. |
| `stop_recording` | Stops it and returns the absolute path of each video file, under `<output>/videos/<session>/` (`.e2e` by default), or the URL of a provider's own recording. |
| Project tools | Every `defineTool` in the agent's `tools` that applies to the target's platform, under its own name; an engine pack such as `mobileTools` adds `open_app`, `swipe`, `alert`. |

Project tools use their `toModelOutput` renderer for strings as well as
structured results. Its `error-text` and `error-json` outputs set the MCP
result's `isError: true`; treat them as failed calls.

`screenshot` masks secure fields only, after a secret fill too (topic
`writing-tests`). Before the session's first `screenshot`, a point tool
(`tap_at`, `hover_at`, `drag_at`, `type_at`, `press_at`, `select_at`) only
says to take one.

Resources: `e2e://guide` and `e2e://guide/<topic>` hold this skill.

## Workflow

1. Read topic `writing-tests` before you write or edit any test
   (`e2e://guide/writing-tests`, or `npx e2e guide writing-tests`); the
   server's instructions and every `open_session` result say so too. Then,
   before `open_session`, create `tests/<feature>.e2e.ts` (its "Structure"
   section) with its imports, the feature's `describe(...)`, a `test(...)`
   titled with the one behavior it verifies, and the call that opens the
   screen it covers, such as `app.open('/settings/members')`. A setup test
   (`test.setup`) goes top-level instead, outside any `describe`.
   Then `open_session`, which opens the app, and go to that screen: on the
   web, `call {tool: "navigate", args: {url: "<the path app.open names>"}}`;
   on a device, the shortest path from the launch screen. Actions that only
   got you there, such as a sign-in the test's saved session replaces, stay
   out of the test when its opening reaches that screen directly; otherwise
   they are its first steps. Node ids are valid only for the newest
   observation; an action reports what changed, so `observe` again before
   using new ids.
2. Walk the flow one screen at a time, and write each screen's steps into
   the file before you leave it. Do not walk the whole flow first and write
   the test from memory afterwards. Each step is one of two kinds:
   - An `agent.act` goal, the default for a path that varies: write the goal
     with the words on screen and its values in `params`, then walk its
     path in the session. Those actions stay out of the test, and so do the
     test lines they print.
   - A `screen` line, for an exact value or interaction: a sign-in form in a
     setup test, a field that must receive one specific string, an
     interaction that is the point of the test. Act on the control by node
     id, then copy the `Test line:` the action printed into the file. Its
     locator matched that control alone on the live screen. When the action
     prints `No test line:` instead, the reason says why; for a control no
     locator found alone, try one with `locate`, or write the line and run
     it with `run_code`.

   With several `screen` steps on one screen, take their actions, then add
   the lines they printed in one edit.
3. When the outcome shows, add its check to the test's assert block, after
   every step: an `agent.assert`, or an `expect` you ran first with
   `call {tool: "run_code", args: {code: "await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveText('Saved');"}}`.
   Build its locator from `observe`, or try it with
   `call {tool: "locate", args: {...}}`. One match: use the printed
   `screen.getByRole(...)` call. Zero or several: adjust before writing it;
   the same failure would hit the test as `LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND` or
   `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS`. A role query's `name` matches the accessible name
   only, while `observe` shows a `status`, `alert`, or `listitem` by its
   text: `status "Saved."` on an unlabelled status is its text, so match it
   with `getByRole('status').filter({ hasText: 'Saved.' })` or `getByText`.

   `run_code` runs statements as a test body writes them, in order, with a
   test's waits and matchers, and stops at the first failure. The
   statements that pass, except reads, join `test_lines` in the order they
   ran. When one fails, fix it from its code and message and the screen in
   the result, then run only the fixed statement and the ones after it:
   the app is where the passing statements left it, so starting over
   repeats their actions. Lines on an engine fixture
   (`expect(browser).toHaveURL(...)`) can't run there; write them from the
   screen, whose header names the current path. In a project with
   credentials or secrets, `run_code` refuses a locator found by part of a
   text, `filter({ hasText })` included: use the exact text instead,
   `getByText('Saved.')`, or `filter({ has: screen.getByText('Offer B') })`
   to pick a row. Raise `timeout` for a slow first `app.open`.

   When the walk ends, the test is written, every line you copied from a
   `Test line:` or ran with `run_code` has run once on the live app, and the
   first run checks the rest. If you missed a line, `test_lines` returns
   every line printed or passed so far, in order, the act goals' paths
   included, for the whole session rather than one test. A walk that goes
   on to a second behavior goes on into a second test in the same
   `describe`, with its own assert block: `navigate` back to the path its
   `app.open` names first, so its lines run from the state the test starts
   in. One walk, in order:

   ```text
   write   tests/members.e2e.ts: imports, describe('members'), test('invites a member as an editor'), app.open('/settings/members')
   call    open_session, then navigate {url: "/settings/members"}   its line is the app.open already written
   edit    + await agent.act('invite {email} as an editor', { params: { email: 'ada@example.test' } });
   call    tap, type, select, tap                   the goal's path; its test lines stay out
   call    run_code {code: "await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toContainText('Invite sent');"}   passed
   edit    + that line, in the assert block
   write   + test('finds a member by name'), app.open('/settings/members')
   call    navigate {url: "/settings/members"}       the new test's fresh start
   call    type {target: "n40", value: "grace"}     prints the test line below
           Test line: await screen.getByRole("searchbox", "Search members").fill("grace");
   edit    + that line, as printed
   call    run_code {code: "await expect(screen.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveCount(1);"}   passed
   edit    + that line, in the assert block
   ```
4. Run only that test:
   `run_tests {files: ["tests/<feature>.e2e.ts:<line>"]}`, or
   `npx e2e run tests/<feature>.e2e.ts:<line>` from the shell (SKILL.md,
   "Rerunning a test while you fix it"). On a failure, fix from the run's failure block
   and the trace page (topic `debugging`), then rerun it the same way. To see a screen the evidence leaves out, go
   straight to it instead of walking the flow again from the start:
   `open_session {test}` stops on the failure screen (Fixing a failing
   test); otherwise, on the web, `navigate` to its path; on a device, the
   shortest path from the launch screen. Then `observe` and `locate`, or
   run the fixed line with `run_code`.
5. Leave the session open through those runs, on the screen under test,
   wherever Rules lets a run go beside it, so step 4's live look needs no
   new session. `observe` does not reload: `navigate` even to the screen
   the session is on when the run or a fix may have changed what it shows.
   A live look's actions print test lines too: copy a fixed line from its
   action, since `test_lines` also lists the looks after the first walk.
   `close_session` once the test passes; an idle session closes on its own
   after 30 minutes and never outlives 4 hours. When the client exits, every
   session closes and the app commands stop. To look at another project or
   config, `open_session {config: "path/to/e2e.config.ts"}` (absolute, or
   relative to the server's working directory); no restart needed.

## Fixing a failing test

When a run's evidence leaves out a screen the fix needs (topic
`debugging`), don't walk the flow again from the start over `call`. A
session runs the test and stops where it failed:

1. `open_session {test: "tests/<feature>.e2e.ts:<line>"}`, where `<line>` is
   the line of the test's `test(` call, not the failing line inside it. A
   file that holds one test needs no line. The test
   runs the way `e2e run` runs it: `beforeAll` and `beforeEach` hooks,
   `test.extend` fixtures, and the body, with the same locators, `expect`,
   and timeouts.
2. Read the text above the session summary: the outcome, the error code and
   message, the failing line with the code around it, the URL, the nodes on
   screen nearest a locator that matched nothing, and the steps that ran.
   The screen below it is the live screen where the test stopped.
3. `observe` and `locate` on that screen to find the right name or the
   missing step. Then carry on from there: act out the test's next lines
   with `call`, so the rerun finds no second mistake. Each action prints the
   `Test line:` that repeats it; where it differs from the test's line, use
   the printed one. Edit the test file. `test_lines` returns the session's lines,
   which start after the test's own.
4. To rerun, `close_session`, then `open_session {test}` again. The session
   loads the config and the test files fresh, so it runs the edited test
   from the start and stops on the next failure, or on the final screen.
5. `close_session`, then confirm once with
   `run_tests {files: ["tests/<feature>.e2e.ts:<line>"]}`.

- `afterEach` hooks and fixture teardown wait for `close_session`; a failure
  there shows as a `Cleanup (afterEach)` line in its result.
- The replay cache treats the test as a run's first attempt: an `agent.act`
  step recorded by `e2e run` or an earlier session replays, and a new one is
  recorded once a later check passes.
- The name follows `e2e run`'s positional rules and must select one test on
  the session's target. Several fail with `TEST_AMBIGUOUS`, which lists them
  as `file:line`; none fails with `NO_TESTS`.
- `SESSION_TEST_UNSUPPORTED`: a test in a serial group, a test that starts
  from a setup test's `session`, and a test that runs as several agents
  can't run alone in a session. Fix those with `run_tests`.

## Rules

- Record a demo or a bug for a pull request with `start_recording` once the
  screen is set up, and `stop_recording` when the part worth watching is
  over; `close_session` saves one still running. Videos are not masked:
  keep secrets off screen while recording.
- A failed action is an error result that leads with the tool, its target,
  and the code (`tap #n9 failed: LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND: ...`) and still shows
  the screen it re-observed: re-aim from that screen.
- Nothing a session does is recorded as a test, and only a test it runs
  (`open_session {test}`) reads or writes the replay cache. A session is for
  looking and trying; the test is the file you write as you walk.
- On the web, a session can stay open while `run_tests` or `e2e run` runs, unless the two
  collide over the app. Read the target's `app`:
  - No `command` (the app runs elsewhere): both use that app.
  - A `url` on port `0`: the session and each run start their own copy of
    the app. A dev server that allows one copy per directory, such as
    `next dev` in Next.js 16, fails the run with `APP_UNREACHABLE`; close
    the session before each run there.
  - A `command` on a fixed port with `reuseExisting: true`: a run uses the
    app the session started, and its data. Whichever started the app stops
    it: if the session closes during a run (`close_session`, 30 idle minutes
    or the 4-hour limit, since a run is not session activity), the app stops
    under the run. Its next navigation fails with `APP_UNREACHABLE`; a step
    already on the page fails with whatever the dead server breaks. Before a
    long run, `observe` once to reset the idle clock. With `CI` set, as in
    many agent sandboxes, `reuseExisting` is ignored: prefix the run with
    `CI=` to unset it, which also drops the other CI defaults (topic
    `running`), or close the session before each run.
  - A `command` on a fixed port without it: a run beside the session fails
    with `APP_ALREADY_RUNNING`. Offer the user `reuseExisting: true` (CI
    ignores it); never add it unasked. Until then, close the session before
    each run.
- On mobile, close the session before each run: a session and a run on one
  device fight over it. It can stay open only on a target whose `device` no
  run uses, with each run passing `--target` for another; an `app.command`
  both start (Metro) follows the web rules above. Ask before adding a
  target to the user's config (topic `setup`).
- Parallel agents (subagents) share one server: each opens its own session
  and passes its session id to every `tools`, `call`, and `close_session`.
  A call may leave `session` out only while one session is open. Sessions
  open at once share one config. Sessions on the same app command share its
  process, which stops when the last of them closes. On mobile, two sessions
  on one simulator fight over it: one target per device (topic `setup`), each
  session on its own target.
- `TARGET_REQUIRED`: pass `target` to `open_session` or start with `--target`.
  `UNKNOWN_TARGET`: no target of that name; the message lists the declared
  ones. `NO_SESSION`: call `open_session` first, or the session named has
  ended (the message says why). `SESSION_REQUIRED`: several sessions are open;
  pass `session`. `SESSION_OPEN`: every session slot is taken (close one, or
  raise `--max-sessions`). `CONFIG_IN_USE`: open sessions use another config,
  or were opened with `engine` and this one names a config; open the same
  way, or close them first. `ENGINE_NOT_INSTALLED`: run the install command
  the message names, or ask the user to when you cannot, then `open_session` again. `ENGINE_IN_USE`: the target's engine
  comes from a package every session shares; create it in the config or a
  file it imports by path. `UNKNOWN_TOOL`: the name is not in this session's
  catalog; the message lists what is. `TEST_AMBIGUOUS` and
  `SESSION_TEST_UNSUPPORTED`: see Fixing a failing test. `RUNNER_BUSY`:
  `run_tests` is already running a suite; wait for its result.

# Running tests

## Contents

- Commands
- The replay cache
- Output
- Exit codes
- Continuous integration

## Commands

```bash
npx e2e run [files...] [options]   # run tests
npx e2e explore [goal] [options]   # explore toward a goal without a test file (topic explore)
npx e2e list [files...] [options]  # print what run would select
npx e2e doctor [--check-model]     # can a run start: config, engine setup, models;
                                   # --json for a host, exit 2 on a failed check
npx e2e init [directory] [--yes]   # scaffold a project, refresh the agent skill
npx e2e guide [topic]              # print this skill; topics: setup, writing-tests, agent,
                                   # running, explore, debugging, mcp, bug-bash
npx e2e cache ls|clear|stats       # inspect or empty the replay cache
npx e2e login|logout|models [provider]  # e2e/oauth subscription logins: openai,
                                   # github-copilot, opencode-console, spacexai
npx e2e mcp [--target <name>]      # MCP server for a coding agent (topic mcp)
npx e2e upgrade [version|tag]      # e2e and its @e2e-dev packages to latest or a version;
                                   # alias update, --dry-run shows the plan; updates
                                   # this skill's copies too; an e2e without the
                                   # command: npx e2e@latest upgrade
npx e2e feedback -m <text> [opts]  # report a problem with e2e itself
npx e2e telemetry [disable|enable] # anonymous usage telemetry: status or switch
```

`run` flags:

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `[files...]` | Files, directories, quoted globs relative to the project root, or a bare name (`signup`, `signup.e2e.ts`, `agent/signup.e2e.ts` all select `tests/agent/signup.e2e.ts`); `file:line` is the test whose `test(` opens on that line. They narrow the config `tests` glob, never bypass it. |
| `--config <path>` | Config file; default `e2e.config.ts` or `.mts`, found upward. |
| `--target <ids>` | Target names, comma-separated or repeated; only these start their app commands. Unknown names fail before startup. |
| `--tag <tags>` | Any of the tags, comma-separated or repeated; all of them with `--tag-mode all`. An empty `--target`, `--tag`, or `--agent` value is a usage error, exit 2. |
| `--exclude-tag <tags>` | Drop tests carrying any of these tags, however selected. |
| `--grep <pattern>`, `--grep-invert <pattern>` | Keep, or drop, tests whose title (describe titles and test title joined by spaces, `checkout pays`; not file or tags) matches a regular expression. Bare pattern or `'/pattern/i'`; repeat for alternatives. |
| `--changed-since <ref>` | Run the configured `filters` on the change since the ref: every file that differs from the merge base of the ref and HEAD, uncommitted and untracked included (`--changed-since origin/main`). Each target starts the files of the tests the filters score likeliest first (`relevance`, see topic `setup`). Without it no filter runs. A ref git can't measure from is `INVALID_CHANGED_SINCE`, exit 2. |
| `--last-failed` | The tests the previous run (`<output>/report.json`) did not pass or never ran (`--max-failures` and `--max-duration` included), plus every test in a failed `beforeAll` or `afterAll` scope. A test another filter leaves out stays owed (`run.carried` in the report) until a rerun runs it. No report is `NO_LAST_RUN`, exit 2. |
| `--shard <index/total>` | One contiguous slice of the selected tests (`--shard 2/3`), cut after every other flag; serial groups stay whole, each shard brings its own setup tests. |
| `--headed` | Visible browser or simulator when the engine supports it. |
| `--agent <names>` | Run unpinned tests as these `agents.<name>` entries (default `agents.default`), comma-separated or repeated; several names run each such test once per agent. |
| `--workers <n>`, `--retries <n>` | Override the resolved values; retries 0-10, workers 1-1024. A retry replays the cache only in strict mode (`--strict-cache`, `cache.strict`); otherwise it runs every agent step live. |
| `--action-timeout <ms>`, `--assertion-timeout <ms>` | Override config `actionTimeout` (default 30000) and `assertionTimeout` (default 5000) for this run; a call's own `{ timeout }` still wins. |
| `--max-failures <n>` | Stop after n failures: the rest skip (cause `failure-limit`), running tests end `interrupted`; exit 1. |
| `--max-duration <ms>` | Stop after ms of running tests, over config `maxDuration`: the rest skip (cause `time-limit`), running tests end `interrupted`, `RUN_TIMEOUT`; exit 1. |
| `--repeat-each <n>` | Run every selected test n times, each run its own result (`repeat` 0 through n-1); add `--no-cache` or later runs replay the first's recording. The `Repeats` summary row names each unstable test's failed runs. |
| `--reporter <ids>` | `list`, `json`, `junit`, `markdown`, comma-separated; `json` cannot combine with `list`. An empty value is a usage error, exit 2. |
| `--output <dir>` | Results directory, over the config's `output` (default `.e2e`). Must be inside the project root, not the root itself (`INVALID_CONFIG`); to keep reports elsewhere, copy them after the run. |
| `--no-cache` | Replay cache off for this run. |
| `--strict-cache` | Fail a step whose committed recording no longer replays (`REPLAY_STALE`, exit 2) instead of handing it to the agent; retries replay too, and the run never writes the cache. |
| `-u`, `--update-snapshots` | Write the stored screenshots `toHaveScreenshot` finds missing or different, and pass. |
| `-w`, `--watch` | Run, then run again when a test file, a source file beside the tests, or the config is saved, or a key asks: `a` or enter all, `r` the current filters, `f` failed, `u` update snapshots, `p` and `t` filter by file and title, `q` quit; a key during a run cancels it. Refused in CI and with `--reporter json`. |
| `--pass-with-no-tests` | Exit 0, not `NO_TESTS`, when nothing matches; a run with nothing to run starts no engine or app. |
| `--step` | Run the first step, then hold each later one until a key at its prompt: Enter runs it, `n` the rest of the test, `a` the rest of the run, `h` lists the keys, `q` stops (exit 130). Without a terminal (an agent's shell) the run goes on in the background and each command returns at the next held step with the screen it waits on: then `e2e run --step next` runs that step, `rest` the rest, `stop` ends the run; run them from the same directory. A shell with a terminal gets the key prompt instead: redirect stdin from the null device (`< /dev/null`, or `< NUL` in Windows `cmd`). Refused in CI, with `--watch`, `--workers` above 1, and the json reporter. |
| `--debug` | Phase timings and an agent step table on stderr; transcripts as artifacts. |
| `--ai-trace` | Every model call except a test filter's, to `<output>/ai-trace.json`. |
| `--timings <file>` | The timings history to update, over `<output>/timings.json`. With more than one worker, files with no recorded time start first, then the rest longest first. |
| `--trace [mode]`, `--video [mode]` | Which tests keep a trace page (`<output>/results/<test>/trace.md`), or which attempts record a video (WebM on browsers, MP4 on devices), over the config and every target: bare is `on` (`--trace` then pages every test, passing ones too); `--trace off` writes none; `retain-on-failure` keeps only failures; `on-first-retry` keeps first retries, `on-all-retries` every retry. A test's own `trace` or `video` still wins; targets whose engine cannot record video are skipped with a notice. Both are greedy: write `--video=<mode>` or put test files first. The failure recap names the trace page and the video. |

```bash
npx e2e run tests/signup.e2e.ts
npx e2e run signup.e2e.ts:12   # by bare name, the test declared at line 12
npx e2e run tests/agent --tag smoke --exclude-tag slow --grep checkout
npx e2e run --last-failed   # the loop after a red run
npx e2e run --changed-since origin/main   # the configured filters judge the change
npx e2e run --shard 2/3     # one CI job of three
npx e2e run 'tests/**/*.smoke.e2e.ts' --target chromium --workers 1 --retries 0
CI=1 npx e2e run            # the CI defaults, locally
```

`list` takes the same files and selection flags (`--config`, `--target`,
`--tag`, `--tag-mode`, `--exclude-tag`, `--grep`, `--grep-invert`,
`--changed-since`, `--last-failed`, `--shard`, `--pass-with-no-tests`),
prints one line per test-target pair, `file › title [target] #tag`, skipped
pairs ending in ` (skipped: <reason>)`, and starts no app, engine, or
worker. With `--changed-since`, the configured filters run as for `run`; a
pair one left out ends in ` (left out by <filter>: <reason>)`. `--reporter json` prints
`{ "pairs": [...] }`, naming a skip or left-out reason `reason` and the
filter that left a pair out `filter`.

`import { list } from 'e2e/runner'` returns that selection plus the pairs a
filter removed, positional arguments that matched no file, and the selected
target names.

```bash
npx e2e list tests/signup.e2e.ts --tag smoke --reporter json
```

`import { run } from 'e2e/runner'` executes the suite and returns its report
without exiting the caller. Pass `cwd`, `config`, and `files` to select the
project and tests, and `changedSince` to run the configured test filters on
the change since that ref;
`onEvent` receives progress and `interruptSignal` cancels
with teardown. A runtime config uses one in-process worker. Await each run
before starting the next and close every host first; overlaps reject with
`RUNNER_BUSY`.

`import { explore } from 'e2e/runner'` runs one exploration the same way:
`cwd`, `config`, `goal`, `target`, `agent`, `session`, `maxSteps`, and
`timeoutMs` as `e2e explore` takes them, plus `onEvent` and
`interruptSignal`. It resolves with the run's result and `explore`, the
record of the steps, findings, and why it ended. A goal or budget out of
range, an unknown target or agent, or an agent with no model rejects before
it starts (`INVALID_CONFIG`, `UNKNOWN_TARGET`, `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`); branch
on `isE2EError(error)` and `error.code`. It shares `run`'s reservation.

With a `package.json` script `"test:e2e": "e2e run"`, pnpm forwards `--`
literally: `pnpm test:e2e -- --headed` reaches e2e as `run -- --headed` and
exits 2. Write `pnpm test:e2e --headed` or `pnpm exec e2e run --headed`.
With npm, use `npm exec -- e2e run --headed` to pass flags to e2e.

## The replay cache

Entries live under `.e2e/cache/`, one file per key, named by key digest.
`E2E_CACHE_DIR` or `--cache-dir <dir>` (on `run` and `cache`) replaces
`cache.dir` (file store only), so worktrees can share one directory; the mode
stays as configured.
`cache` commands read the same config as `run` (`--config`, `cache.dir`);
with a custom `cache.store` they refuse (exit 2), inspect that store with
its own tools.

| Command | Prints |
| --- | --- |
| `e2e cache ls` | One row per entry: test, target, instruction digest, age, action count. |
| `e2e cache stats` | Directory, entry count, total size. |
| `e2e cache clear` | Deletes the entries and the directory; files the runner never wrote stay. |

## Output

`<output>` (`.e2e` by default) holds `report.json`, `junit.xml`,
`summary.md`, `ai-trace.json`, `timings.json` (how long each file took; with more than one worker the next run starts the longest known files first, after any with no time), `sessions/`, and `results/`, one directory
per test with its `trace.md` and an `attempt-<n>/` per attempt
(screenshots, videos, `--debug` transcripts, downloads).
`results/` is cleared once a run's tests start; a run stopping before
leaves the last run's files, and a `--last-failed` rerun keeps the files
the report it reruns names and writes its own under each test's `rerun-<n>/`. The report records every artifact path, a
hosted service's video by URL.

- `list` (default): setup steps, one line per file and target (when stdout
  is not a terminal, each test also prints as it finishes), a `Failed
  Tests` section (error, code, failing line, code frame), then the
  summary rows `Test Files`, `Tests`, `AI`, `Cache` (when the replay cache
  ran), `Repeats` (with `--repeat-each`), `Errors`, `Start at`, `Duration`,
  `Traces` (when a page was written), `Screenshots` (the first 10
  `app.screenshot` files, then a count), `AI trace` (with `--ai-trace`), and
  last `Failed`, one entry per failed test (file and line, error's first
  line, trace page when written), so `| tail` keeps it. Past a minute `Duration`
  repeats as minutes and seconds, setup time split out as `startup` in the
  same parenthetical (`682.97s (11m 23s, startup 43.00s)`).
- `report.json`, for scripts rather than reading (`jq`, CI tools; a reader
  takes the terminal and the trace pages), the one record of every result,
  passing ones included, written whatever the reporters, holds `run.status`,
  `run.exitCode`, `run.errors[]` (run-level, such as `APP_UNREACHABLE`),
  and `run.results[]`, one per test and target: `titlePath`, `file`,
  `source`, `tags` (`[]` when none), `agent`, `repeat` (0 unless
  `--repeat-each`), `selected`, `status`, `attempts[]` of `steps[]`,
  `artifacts[]`, `error`. `run.summary` counts the selected results:
  `passed`, `failed` (timed out included), `interrupted` (stopped by the
  run: a signal, `--max-failures`, `--max-duration`, a run-level error; not a failure), `flaky`, and `skipped` add up
  to `selected`; `discovered - selected` were left out.
- `junit`: `junit.xml` for CI summaries; `--reporter list,junit` keeps the
  terminal output. A case with a failure screenshot links it as
  `<system-out>[[ATTACHMENT|<path>]]</system-out>`, relative to
  `$CI_PROJECT_DIR` (else the project root), which GitLab shows in the
  test report.
- Every run that reaches its tests also writes a trace page per failed,
  timed-out, interrupted, or flaky test, `results/<test>/trace.md` (the
  `trace` mode, default `retain-on-failure`): every step with what
  it did, the cache's decisions, what the app logged, the last model turns,
  and the screen at failure. The `list` output names it under each failure
  (`❯ trace <path>`). Read it first.
- `markdown` (`--reporter list,markdown`): `summary.md` with counts and
  spend, a block per failed test linked to its page, the flaky tests folded
  alike, and every test as one folded table (or an exploration's findings
  and assessment). Paste it into a pull request or handoff.
- `json`: the report on stdout.
- Custom reporters get step progress with `identity` (`attemptId`,
  `attemptIndex`, `stepId`, `stepIndex`: report IDs, zero-based indexes;
  retries change the attempt, serial members share the group's attempt with
  distinct step IDs) and an `end` phase carrying the redacted error and the
  `blocked` and `cancelled` statuses. Older streams may lack `identity`.
- `github()` from `@e2e-dev/github`: on GitHub Actions, one pull request
  comment per run (edited on rerun) plus the job summary; needs
  `pull-requests: write` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` (or `GH_TOKEN`) in the step's
  env.
- `htmlReporter()` from `@e2e-dev/html-reporter`: `<output>/report.html`
  (`.e2e/` by default), one page that opens from disk, with each test's
  steps, screenshots, and video. It links media from `<output>/results/`;
  `media: 'embed'` puts it in the page, one file to share, except downloads
  the runner could not scan for secrets, and `media: 'none'` leaves it out.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| ---: | --- |
| 0 | Every selected test passed, was flaky, or was skipped |
| 1 | A test or setup test failed or timed out |
| 2 | CLI, config, collection, credential, model-config, or policy error |
| 3 | Engine, app process, model provider, artifact, or cleanup failure |
| 4 | Internal runner error |
| 130 | Interrupted by an external signal |

The highest code present wins (`130 > 4 > 3 > 2 > 1 > 0`). 130 needs an
external signal: a `--max-failures` or `--max-duration` stop or a run-level error that
interrupted workers keeps the failures' or the error's code. Exit 2 is
deterministic, never retry it; only exit 3 is worth a job-level retry.

The first SIGINT or SIGTERM interrupts and writes the report if any test
had started; the second forces engine teardown and still writes the
report, plus `junit.xml` and `summary.md` when those reporters are on; the
third kills the app process groups and exits 130 at once.

## Continuous integration

CI mode is on when `CI` is set (not `0` or `false`): `retries` 1,
`workers` 1, `test.only` rejected with
`ONLY_IN_CI`, the replay cache `read-only` unless the config sets a mode explicitly
(`cache: 'read-write'` or `cache.mode`), `reuseExisting` ignored.

`npx e2e init --yes --ci github-actions` writes a workflow like this one with
a job per platform the config's targets run on (web, iOS, Android), for the
project's package manager and model key; `--ci gitlab` writes the same jobs as
`.gitlab-ci.yml` (or `.gitlab/e2e.gitlab-ci.yml` to include beside an existing
one), its mobile jobs on self-managed runners. The mobile jobs build an Expo or
bare React Native app; for any other app, replace the failing build step. It
leaves existing pipeline files alone. Set `app.command` in the config so the
runner starts the app.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/e2e.yml
# Omits the github() reporter: it needs pull-requests: write and
# GITHUB_TOKEN in the run step's env.
name: e2e
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@9fd676a19091d4595eefd76e4bd31c97133911f1 # v4.2.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 26 # Node >= 24.8, or >= 22.22.3 on 22
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
          key: playwright-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml') }}
      - run: pnpm exec e2e-web install chromium --with-deps
      - run: npx e2e run --reporter list,junit
        env:
          AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY }}
          E2E_USER_ADMIN_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.E2E_USER_ADMIN_USERNAME }}
          E2E_USER_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.E2E_USER_ADMIN_PASSWORD }}
      - if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: e2e-report
          path: |
            .e2e/report.json
            .e2e/junit.xml
          if-no-files-found: warn
      - if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: e2e-artifacts
          path: .e2e/results
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7
```

- Install browsers as their own step so the download stays out of the
  launch timeout.
- Upload artifacts unless cancelled, so a test that failed then passed on
  retry keeps its evidence.
- Start the app through the target's `app.command`; the runner tears it down
  on every exit path.
- Agent steps run in the same job: pass the key the config's model reads
  (`AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` for `gateway()` from `ai`) as a secret in the run
  step's `env`, and commit `.e2e/cache/` so recorded steps replay with no
  model call.
- To run only the tests a pull request can affect, install
  `@e2e-dev/decision ai`, add
  `filters: [decisionFilter({ model: gateway.decisionModel('typesafe-ai/jev') })]`
  with `decisionFilter` from `@e2e-dev/decision` and `gateway` from `ai`,
  pass `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` in the run step's `env`, give
  `actions/checkout` `fetch-depth: 0`, and run
  `npx e2e run ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('--changed-since origin/{0}', github.base_ref) || '' }}`.
  Filters run only with `--changed-since <ref>`, which that expression
  passes on `pull_request` alone; never pass it on `pull_request_target`.
  Every test runs without it and on a `--last-failed` rerun. The decision
  filter also runs every test on a lockfile or `e2e.config` change, and the
  tests whose test file, setup file, or stored screenshots changed. It scores
  each test, and each target starts the likeliest files first. With one worker
  (the CI default) only the relevance bands order files and collection order
  breaks ties, since the timings history matters only above one worker. On GitLab, pass `--changed-since ${CI_MERGE_REQUEST_TARGET_BRANCH_SHA:-$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_DIFF_BASE_SHA}`
  on merge request pipelines, not merge trains, with `GIT_DEPTH: 0`. Preview
  with `npx e2e list --changed-since origin/main`, after committing: the
  decision filter reads what the commits change, and a file only the
  working tree changes by name alone.
  Reference: https://e2e.com/docs/filters
